Muradin.synergy_text: Being able to follow up on Muradin's Storm Bolt with a devastating burst damage combo is what makes Mages (for example Li-Ming) his ideal partners. Chaining crowd control Abilities one after another is so valuable in this game that having another Hero who can provide this kind of effects from another Role (such as Blaze played as Offlaner) in your team will make Muradin a real threat for the enemy team.
Muradin.counter_text: Heroes who can deal percent-based damage (such as Tychus via Minigun) can shred Muradin's Health very quickly, especially while in Avatar. When played quick enough, crowd control Abilities (for example Face Melt by E.T.C.) puts a lot of pressure on him because they can stop Dwarf Toss, his only form of escape.
Muradin.maps_text: Muradin's stronger maps Muradin's average maps Muradin's weaker maps In the hand of experienced players, Muradin is good on Maps where he can use his innate resilience and mobility to harass enemy Heroes and enable plays for his entire team by aggressively but safely invading the enemy side of the Map during the early game (such as Hanamura Temple). On the other hand, he is bad on Maps where the Objective takes a long period of time (for example Braxis Holdout) because he will eventually run out of Mana, effectively denying his Trait value.
Muradin.tips: Storm Bolt should be used with patience and combined with the Slow provided by Thunder Clap when possible. Thunder Clap is a decent peeling tool, especially against melee Heroes who rely on Basic Attacks. Dwarf Toss allows you to disengage when low Health, but be careful when the enemy Heroes have crowd control. Avatar is a maximum Health boost that protects you from burst damage but makes you vulnerable to percent-based damage. Haymaker should mostly be used for peeling away enemy Heroes rather than to engage by pushing enemy Heroes towards your team. See our Abilities page for further information »
Muradin.meta_text: Muradin is a well-rounded Tank that can provide vision, engage, and peeling to his team. Thanks to Dwarf Toss allowing him to quickly escape when in danger, Muradin can easily scout the enemy side of the battlefield to give his team a vision advantage, but only if the enemy team does not have tools to easily stop Dwarf Toss during its animation. During team fights, Storm Bolt and Thunder Clap are decent crowd control tools that can be used to either engage enemy Heroes or peel for allied Heroes.

abilities.title: Storm Bolt
abilities.text: Throw a hammer, dealing 110 (+4% per level) damage to the first enemy hit and Stunning them for 1.25 seconds Quest: Basic Attack Heroes affected by Stuns, Slows, or Roots. Slowed or Rooted enemies grant 1 stack. Stunned enemies provide 2 stacks. If the Hero dies within 3 seconds, gain 5 stacks. Reward: Upon hitting 45 targets, Storm Bolt pierces to hit an additional target, and Muradin's Basic Attacks reduce the cooldown of Storm Bolt by 0.5 seconds and restore 3 Mana. Mythic Reward: Upon hitting 160 targets, Storm Bolt's range is increased by 50%, width increased by 100%, and now pierces all targets. Storm Bolt is a Basic Ability which provides Muradin a ranged Stun. As a Muradin player, you should take your time to closely watch how enemy Heroes are moving because this Ability has a small delay and the projectile is not that fast, making it hard to connect if you do not predict the target's movement, assuming they are trying to juke you. Generally speaking, you should avoid using Storm Bolt on high-mobility Heroes if there are other good targets to use it on because there is a high chance you will miss them and thus waste an important cooldown.

abilities.title: Thunder Clap
abilities.text: Blast nearby enemies for 96 (+4% per level) damage and Slow them by 30% for 2.5 seconds. Heroes hit also have their Attack Speed reduced by 30% for the duration. Thunder Clap is a Basic Ability that Slows, reduces the Attack Speed, and deals damage to every enemy in a small radius around Muradin. You can use this Ability to lower the chances to miss Storm Bolt thanks to the Slow provided and/or to reduce the damage done by enemy Heroes who heavily rely on Basic Attacks do deal damage.

abilities.title: Dwarf Toss
abilities.text: Leap to target location, dealing 59 (+4% per level) damage to enemies on landing. Upon leaping, gain 30 Armor for 2 seconds, reducing damage taken by 30%. Dwarf Toss is a Basic Ability that allows Muradin to quickly change position, to either reach enemy Heroes or run away from them. Whether to use it aggressively or defensively depends on the situation. When you are in danger, use it to escape or to gain Armor (for example when Kael'thas uses Pyroblast on you). A good trick to suddenly reach safety is to leap over impassable terrain, especially useful when trying to escape from enemy Heroes who do not have such tool. When your team is in danger, use it to peel. While it does not provide any peeling on its own, it allows you quickly reposition near allied Heroes who need help. When your team wants to force a team fight, use it to engage. While it slightly increases your survivability by giving you Armor, be extremely careful when choosing to do so because you will not have your escape anymore. Before doing aggressive plays like this, always check the Minimap to see if your team is close enough to follow you immediately, else you will end up dying alone for no reason, and make sure your team is ready to follow-up for securing a kill.

abilities.title: Avatar
abilities.text: Avatar (R) Muradin Heroic Transform for 20 seconds, gaining 1000 Health. Avatar is a Heroic Ability that increases Muradin's maximum Health for 20 seconds. The additional Health he immediately receive acts as a form of burst healing that helps him to survive when being focused by the enemy team. The exact moment when to use it depends on how you expect the fight to go. Do not use it too early, else the enemy team will just disengage and wait for it to expire. Do not use it too late, else the enemy team will crowd control you to death before you will be able to cast it.

abilities.title: Haymaker
abilities.text: Haymaker (R) Muradin Heroic Stun target enemy Hero, and wind up a punch dealing 319 (+4% per level) damage and knocking the target back, hitting enemies in the way for 319 (+4% per level) damage and knocking them aside. Haymaker is a Heroic Ability that should usually be used to push dangerous enemy Heroes far from your team as a form of peeling or as an interrupt for dangerous Abilities, however, it can occasionally be used to push vulnerable enemy Heroes towards your team as a form of engage.

abilities.title: Second Wind
abilities.text: Passive Muradin restores 55 (+4% per level) Health per second when he has not taken damage for 4 seconds. When below 40% Health, increased to 111 (+4% per level) Health per second. Second Wind is a Trait that allows Muradin to quickly regenerate his Health when not taking damage. Experienced players will get a lot of value out of it by constantly harassing enemy Heroes during the early game, while scouting and stopping rotations, and during team fights, by getting out for a few seconds while extremely low on Health only to heal up and go in again when at medium/high Health. The ability to passively heal yourself between fights allows you to stay on the battlefield for long periods of time. That said, while you will never need to use your Hearthstone to regenerate your Health, your Mana will eventually reach critical values and force you away from the battlefield for a while.

abilities.title: Baseline Quest
abilities.text: Muradin has a Baseline Quest which requires to hit enemy Heroes with Basic Attacks while they are affected by a Stun, Root, or Slow. You also get 5 stacks when an enemy Hero dies within 3 seconds of being hit by Storm Bolt. Upon reaching 45 stacks, Storm Bolt can pierce the first target hit and Muradin's Basic Attacks restore 3 Mana and reduce the cooldown of Storm Bolt by 0.5 seconds. Upon reaching 160 stacks, you unlock the Mythic Reward: Storm Bolt's range is increased by 50% and width is increased by 100%, and pierces all targets. The first Reward allows you to Stun 2 enemy Heroes if they happen to be lined up, to cast Storm Bolt more often if you have an enemy to hit with Basic Attacks and the enemy team has no Blinds, or simply to Stun an enemy Hero who is hiding behind another enemy (usually a Minion, Summon, or Monster). Last but not the least, you can also use Basic Attacks on any enemy to restore a small amount of Mana. If you use Storm Bolt while far away from your target, you will only be able to get 2 stacks per cast. If you use Storm Bolt while your target is within range of your Basic Attacks and your Basic Attacks are not on cooldown, you will have enough time to hit them with 2 Basic Attacks while they are Stunned and therefore gain 4 stacks per cast. While it will not always be possible to cast Storm Bolt in melee range, it is good to be aware of this interaction. The best way to get stacks on your own is to roam on the battlefield and find isolated enemy Heroes to harass them with Thunder Clap, Storm Bolt, and Basic Attacks. You generally want to keep Dwarf Toss off cooldown and only use it to escape, ideally over impassable terrain because a lot of Heroes cannot follow you over it. The best way to get stacks with the help of your team is to have an allied Hero with a Stun to use as follow-up to Storm Bolt (for example Tyrande with Lunar Flare). Since the target will be Stunned for longer, you will get double stacks per Basic Attacks for longer. When doing so, make sure to wait for their cooldown to be back before using Storm Bolt again.

Murky.name: Murky
Murky.overview: Murky is a Melee Assassin that excels at frustrating his opponents. Uniquely designed, he is adept at attracting the attention of enemy players, causing them to behave inefficiently to respond to his abrasive presence. Murky's allies must capitalise on the fact that he thrives in attrition battles; even if his attributes and damage values are limited, his Hero Trait, Spawn Egg, makes it so that he is never away from battle for long when killed.
strengths: Strong revival mechanic in the form of Spawn Egg
Has access to Octo-Grab, one of the strongest Heroic Abilities in the game
weaknesses: Extremely fragile; by far the lowest amount of Health amongst all Heroes
Inept at carrying coin-like Objectives, which are dropped on death
Several conditions may limit his damage potential
Distinct playstyle to which your team must adapt

build_notes.name: Slime Build
build_notes.text: Murky's Slime Build is designed to increase his survivability during team fights, especially if he happens to hit multiple enemies with Slime. This allows Murky to be quite annoying when he does not get killed quickly. In order to stack Slime Time at Level 4, try to hit enemy Heroes with Slime when there are no enemy Minions to clear. The range from Black Lagoon at Level 7 makes it easier to hit enemy Heroes with Slime. Toxic Buildup at Level 16 and Making Inky at Level 20 increase your damage output. Pufferfish Build Advanced Murky's Pufferfish Build is designed to empower your waveclear and, more in general, your macro impact on the game. This allows Murky to put a lot of pressure on the enemy team outside of team fights. Tufferfish at Level 4 increases your waveclear. Fish Oil at Level 16 allows you to clear Minions by just using Pufferfish. Faster Fish at Level 20 makes Pufferfish more reliable against enemy Heroes.

build_notes.text: Murky's ARAM Build is designed to increase his survivability during team fights, especially if he happens to hit multiple enemies with Slime. This allows Murky to be quite annoying when he does not get killed quickly. In order to stack Slime Time at Level 4, try to hit enemy Heroes with Slime when there are no enemy Minions to clear. The range from Black Lagoon at Level 7 makes it easier to hit enemy Heroes with Slime. Toxic Buildup at Level 16 and Making Inky at Level 20 increase your damage output. Murky.synergy_text: Murky's small Health pool benefits from any effect that can mitigate incoming damage (for example Blinds, Armor, or Shields).
Murky.counter_text: Murky's predictable attack plan and his dependency on remaining within close range of his targets to effectively deal damage make him vulnerable to most high damage Hero with some way of kiting him or quickly destroying Pufferfish.
Murky.maps_text: Murky's stronger maps Murky's average maps Murky's weaker maps Murky needs to scale for being impactful in team fights and that Murky's main strengths in the early game are gank resistance and waveclear. As such, Murky does great on late game Maps, especially if it possible to double soak, and does poorly on early game Maps. Since one of Murky's main strengths is the ability to quickly respawn from Spawn Egg, he is not a great choice on Maps where the Objective consists of items that need to be collected and are lost on death (Coins on Blackheart's Bay, Gems on Tomb of the Spider Queen, Warheads on Warhead Junction) because they require you to play safe.
Murky.tips: Hide your Spawn Egg in nooks and crannies, bushes, or near allied Structures so that it is difficult to find. Use Slime and Pufferfish to efficiently waveclear at all stages of the game. Standing on top of Pufferfish will prevent opponents from targeting it easily. Try and dodge dangerous skillshots or area of effect Abilities with Safety Bubble. Call out your intended Octo-Grab target so that your teammates know just who to focus down. See our Abilities page for further information »
Murky.meta_text: Murky's primary team fighting goal is to single-out key opponents for quick, one-sided kills. He also conditionally deals a fair amount of area of effect damage, however, most of his damage can be avoided by playing in a particularly defensive way. This peculiar aspect is made up for by the facts that Murky can revive and come back to an ongoing fight nearly instantly, thanks to his Spawn Egg Ability. Because of this, any energy spent killing Murky is inefficiently used, and one should see to capitalise on this attribute to take pressure away from allies. This makes him especially strong against team compositions that lack reliable targeted burst damage. Outside of combat, Murky has some of the best waveclear available, and can scout where it would be dangerous for any other Hero to do so.

abilities.title: Slime
abilities.text: Deal 86 (+4% per level) damage and apply Slime on nearby enemies for 6 seconds, Slowing them by 20%. Deal 210 (+4% per level) damage to enemies who are already Slimed. Structures take 50% damage. Slime is Murky's bread and butter. As such, it should aggressively be used on-cooldown whenever you are in range of anything hostile. In lane, it is possible to hit an entire wave of Minions by placing yourself directly on top of the Wizard Minion. When used against enemy Heroes, the Slow provided is useful at all stages of the game for body blocking, as its long uptime allows you to remain in front of your target. When used against enemy Structures, it only deals 50% damage. An important aspect of Slime to consider is that its damage is significantly increased against foes that have already been afflicted by its lengthy effect. You should always try to repeatedly hit Slimed targets so as to benefit from it.

abilities.title: Pufferfish
abilities.text: Spit out a Pufferfish with 225 (+5.5% per level) health at the target point. After 2.75 seconds, the fish will blow up for 330 (+4% per level) damage. Deals 50% less damage to Structures. Quest: Kill Slimed Enemies or hit them with Pufferfish. Heroes and Structures award 4 bonus stacks. Reward: After obtaining 200 stacks, Murky's Basic Abilities no longer deal reduced damage to structures. Mythic Reward: After obtaining 400 stacks, Murky's health is increased by 50%. Pufferfish is one of the hardest-hitting Abilities in the game. It is, however, difficult to successfully hit individual foes with it. When it is not sidestepped, it might just see itself destroyed. During team fights, it is important to try and cast Pufferfish where it is unlikely to be killed by incidental area of effect damage. This generally means somewhere between your opponents' frontline and backline, and never on top of your own teammates. While laning, one way of preventing your opponents from attacking the Pufferfish is to self-cast it by pressing [Alt + Q] and not move to stand directly on top of it, making clicking through to attack it harder. You can also hide it in bushes, to surprise enemy Heroes who are right outside but still within Pufferfish range. This trick is possible because an exploding Pufferfish in a bush is only visible to the enemy team if they have vision inside that bush.

abilities.title: Safety Bubble
abilities.text: Becomes Invulnerable for 2 seconds. While active, Murky cannot attack or use abilities. Safety Bubble is Murky's main defensive Ability. Since it renders him completely invulnerable, and instantly so, it can be used to avoid dangerous incoming Abilities. A less-known aspect of the Ability is that it can also be used to disjoint inbound projectiles, such as those from Basic Attacks. The fact that it removes movement-impairing effects (as well as providing a temporary immunity to them) can be used offensively, allowing you to move through lingering area effects that would stop other Heroes in their tracks. Murky players become extremely difficult to peel off when tracking the cooldown of strong crowd control Abilities to completely avoid them with Safety Bubble.

abilities.title: March of the Murlocs
abilities.text: March of the Murlocs (R) Murky Heroic After 0.75 seconds, Murky commands a legion of Murlocs to march in a target direction, each one leaping onto the first enemy Hero or Structure they find. Each Murloc deals 130 (+4% per level) damage and slows its target by 15% for 5 seconds. Murlocs deal 50% damage to Structures. To balance out to its immense damage potential, March of the Murlocs is very easy for your opponents to avoid. Due to its very long cooldown, it is typically only used in major team fights that occur around Structures or Objectives, as to force opponents to either potentially face a large amount of damage, or let go of the contested element. It can also be used to completely block off a potential escape route.

abilities.title: Octo-Grab
abilities.text: Octo-Grab (R) Murky Heroic Murky becomes Unstoppable and Stuns target enemy Hero for 3 seconds while he hits them for 1 damage a second. Octo-Grab is the longest targeted Stun in the game. It is almost always used right after placing Pufferfish to guarantee a large amount of damage. The most reliable way of preventing Octo-Grab from being used as a way of locking down kill targets is to use cleanse effects (for example Intercession by Whitemane), as well as a few other select Heroic Abilities ( Crystal Aegis, Divine Shield, and Sanctification) and Talents. It is therefore essential that you learn to track the cooldown of those Abilities, lest Octo-Grab could end up being partly or completely countered. Another alternative is to aim, with the help of your teammates, for the Heroes that do have access to cleanse effects (for example Intercession by Whitemane) or similar tools to deal with crowd control effects.

abilities.title: Spawn Egg
abilities.text: Place an Egg at target location, revealing the nearby area. Upon dying, Murky respawns at the Egg after 8 seconds. Murky only grants 25% of a real Hero's experience upon dying. If Murky's Egg is killed, he is revealed to enemies for 15 seconds, and Spawn Egg is placed on cooldown. Spawn Egg is what makes Murky unique, and the main factor that separates good Murky players from outstanding ones, depending on where it is placed and moved during the game. After 5 seconds of not taking damage, Murky's Egg starts regenerating 42 Health per second (scaling), so the opponents have to ideally destroy it in one go if they want to avoid wasting time. Upon reviving from an Egg, Murky gains a Shield equal to 35% of his maximum Health for 15 seconds. The fact that Murky only yields 25% of a normal Hero's Experience upon death makes it so that, essentially, efforts spent to kill him are poorly invested. As a Murky player, your main goal is to exploit this fact to take as much pressure as possible away from your allies. Willingly absorbing skillshots, aggressively body blocking, or bullying vulnerable enemy Heroes so as to force a response are all legitimate manners of imposing your presence. Another important aspect to consider is that Murky's respawn time from his Egg is only 8 seconds at all stages of the game. Early on, this advantage is mediocre; later in the game, it is outstanding. Furthermore, the time it takes you to travel back to points of contention, Objectives, allied Structures that need to be defended, or general team fights, is entirely dependent on how aggressively you decide to position your Egg. Spawn Egg rewards selective aggressivity.

abilities.title: Baseline Quest
abilities.text: Murky has a Baseline Quest which requires to kill Slimed enemies or to hit Slimed enemies with Pufferfish. Heroes and Structures give 4 additional stacks. Upon reaching 200 stacks, Murky's Basic Abilities no longer deal 50% less damage to Structures. Upon reaching 400 stacks, you unlock the Mythic Reward: Murky's maximum Health is increased by 50%. This means that Murky will be harder to kill. In order to get the highest amount of stacks possible from enemy Minions, you need to hit them with Pufferfish while they are Slimed. This way each Minion within Slime range will give you 1 stack for killing a Slimed enemy and 1 stack for hitting a Slimed enemy with Pufferfish. If you cast Pufferfish too late or it gets destroyed by opponents, you will gain fewer stacks in the process.

opts.name: Fish Eye
opts.text: Spawning from his Egg increases Murky's mount speed to 45% for 5 seconds. Passive: Increase the Egg's Health by 100%, its sight radius by 300%, and it reveals all enemies in its sight radius.

opts.name: Shell Game
opts.text: Murky can now place 2 Eggs and will randomly revive from them, however, the cooldown of placing an Egg is increased by 15 seconds.

opts.name: A Fishy Deal
opts.text: Killing a Minion with Pufferfish grants a stack of Bribe. Use 8 stacks to bribe a Mercenary, instantly defeating them. Does not work on Elite Mercenaries. Maximum of 32 stacks of Bribe.

opts.name: Slime Time
opts.text: Quest: Slime enemy Heroes that are already Slimed. Reward: After Sliming 10 Heroes, increase Slime's bonus damage by 125. Reward: After Sliming 20 Heroes, increase Slime's slow amount to 30%.

opts.name: Tufferfish
opts.text: Pufferfish gains 50 Spell Armor and deals 50% more damage to Slimed targets.

opts.name: Living the Dream
opts.text: Quest: Every 15 seconds Murky is alive, he gains 5% Spell Power, up to 25%. This bonus is reset upon his death.

opts.name: Black Lagoon
opts.text: Increase Slime's radius by 30%.

opts.name: Slippery When Wet
opts.text: Gain 50% Movement Speed and move through units while in Safety Bubble. Additionally, Safety Bubble's cooldown is reduced by 2 seconds.

opts.name: Time to Krill
opts.text: Basic Attacks against Heroes deal an additional 7 (+4% per level) damage a second and slow the target by 7% for 4 seconds. This effect can stack up to 5 times.

opts.name: March of the Murlocs
opts.text: Cooldown: 90 seconds After 0.75 seconds, Murky commands a legion of Murlocs to march in a target direction, each one leaping onto the first enemy Hero or Structure they find. Each Murloc deals 130 (+4% per level) damage and slows its target by 15% for 5 seconds. Murlocs deal 50% damage to Structures.

opts.name: Octo-Grab
opts.text: Cooldown: 50 seconds Murky becomes Unstoppable and Stuns target enemy Hero for 3 seconds while he hits them for 1 damage a second.

opts.name: Rejuvenating Bubble
opts.text: Safety Bubble restores 40% of Murky's maximum Health.

opts.name: Egg Shell
opts.text: Upon casting Spawn Egg, or when one of his eggs is killed, Murky gains a Shield for an amount equal to 50% of Murky's current Health.

opts.name: Fish Tank
opts.text: Murky is healed for 20% of the damage he deals with Basic Attacks and Basic Abilities.

opts.name: Toxic Buildup
opts.text: Every 3rd consecutive Basic Attack against an enemy Hero causes a free Slime to be cast upon them.

opts.name: Fish Oil
opts.text: The Pufferfish casts Slime at its location upon landing.

opts.name: Wrath of Cod
opts.text: Heroes hit by Pufferfish take additional damage equal to 16% of their maximum Health over 4 seconds.

opts.name: Never-Ending Murlocs
opts.text: March of the Murlocs can be channeled indefinitely, and will always last its base duration when canceled early. In addition, it no longer deals reduced damage to Structures.

opts.name: ... And a Shark Too!
opts.text: Increase the damage of Octo-Grab by 13700%.

opts.name: Making Inky
opts.text: Reduces the cooldown of Slime by 1.5 seconds.

opts.name: Faster Fish
opts.text: Pufferfish explodes 1.5 seconds faster.

pairs.text: Fenix Murky Murky can go around alone and use Octo-Grab on isolated enemy Heroes to keep them in place for Fenix that will use Planet Cracker as follow-up. When alone, enemy Heroes cannot break Pufferfish to take less damage during Octo-Grab. Since Murky respawns faster than other Heroes when having Spawn Egg somewhere, he is not worried to be alone on the battlefield.

Nazeebo.name: Nazeebo
Nazeebo.overview: Nazeebo is a Mage able to deal a good amount of burst damage and a decent amount of sustained damage from the distance, provided with some crowd control and a high Health pool. While his damage looks decent at any stage of the game, Nazeebo becomes a real threat only in the late game.
strengths: Unique crowd control via Zombie Wall

build_notes.name: Zombie Wall Build
build_notes.text: Nazeebo's Zombie Wall Build combines a bit more safety with high damage output against enemy Heroes who cannot play around Zombie Wall by using their own Abilities or with the help of allied Heroes. The increased casting range provided by Thing of the Deep at Level 1 helps Nazeebo hit enemies with his Abilities, especially Zombie Wall, and gives him extra safety at any stage of the game, unless dove. While his early game damage is not that great, the additional Spell Power provided empowers both his Heroic Abilities, something that will compensate this little weakness during big team fights in the later stages of the game. Attention! Once you reach Level 20, if you are too far from having 175 stacks of Voodoo Ritual, do not pick Vile Infection because it would do nothing. Upgrade your Heroic Ability instead. Corpse Spiders Build Advanced Nazeebo's Corpse Spiders Build focuses on Corpse Spiders, which provides him with outstanding burst damage. Choose this Build when you need to take down an enemy Hero as fast as possible, especially if they dive on your team but also when your Tank has a short-range engage that can be used to crowd control a target and allow you to easily follow-up with all of your Abilities.

build_notes.name: Plague of Toads Build
build_notes.text: Nazeebo's Plague of Toads Build is all about poke damage with Plague of Toads, to pressure the enemy Healer and win the team fight by attrition without exposing too much. If you are playing on a Map where the Objective is valuable and takes over 30 seconds to be secured by one of the teams, this Build may be an option against some team compositions who lack sustain healing and cannot engage aggressively. Attention! Once you reach Level 20, if you are too far from having 175 stacks of Voodoo Ritual, do not pick Vile Infection because it would do nothing. Upgrade your Heroic Ability instead.

build_notes.name: ARAM Build
build_notes.text: Nazeebo's ARAM Build combines a bit more safety with high damage output against enemy Heroes who cannot play around Zombie Wall by using their own Abilities or with the help of allied Heroes. The increased casting range provided by Thing of the Deep at Level 1 helps Nazeebo hit enemies with his Abilities, especially Zombie Wall, and gives him extra safety at any stage of the game, unless dove. While his early game damage is not that great, the additional Spell Power provided empowers both his Heroic Abilities, something that will compensate this little weakness during big team fights in the later stages of the game. Attention! Once you reach Level 20, if you are too far from having 175 stacks of Voodoo Ritual, do not pick Vile Infection because it would do nothing. Upgrade your Heroic Ability instead. See our Talents page for further information » Create your own build and share it with friends!

Nazeebo.synergy_text: In order to make Nazeebo work, we recommend picking a Marksman (such as Sylvanas) to guarantee your team a good damage output when your Abilities are on cooldown and a Tank who can provide crowd control (such as Mal'Ganis) that Nazeebo will be able to follow up with Zombie Wall. There are also some Healers who can get value from Zombie Wall after it spawns, usually by adding crowd control (for example Auriel using Detainment Strike).
Nazeebo.counter_text: Nazeebo is countered by Heroes who can punish his weak early game (such as Sylvanas that can enable her team to push by using Haunting Arrows to disable Structures) and he is rendered almost useless by Heroes who can easily get out from Zombie Wall and eventually dodge his other Abilities (for example E.T.C. can use Face Melt to Knockback the Zombies surrounding himself or a nearby allied Hero).
Nazeebo.maps_text: Nazeebo's stronger maps Nazeebo's average maps Nazeebo's weaker maps Nazeebo requires to rotate between two lanes in order to gather stacks for Voodoo Ritual as quickly as possible and eventually unlock Vile Infection at Level 20. As a consequence, he is good on Maps where it is fast and safe to rotate between lanes (such as rotating mid-top on Tomb of the Spider Queen) and he should not be picked on Maps where it is impossible to rotate because there are only 2 lanes (like Braxis Holdout), where it is slow and/or dangerous to rotate between lanes (for example Cursed Hollow), or on mid-game Maps where there is a low chance to reach Level 20 (such as Sky Temple).
Nazeebo.tips: If you last-hit a Minion with Corpse Spiders, the Spiders can potentially run towards a nearby Hero. Zombie Wall can be used to tank Structures. Considering that Plague of Toads can be difficult to hit, use it on enemy Heroes coming towards you. When the Objective is not active, focus on Voodoo Ritual to unlock Vile Infection in the late game. See our Abilities page for further information »
Nazeebo.meta_text: Nazeebo is the Mage with the second highest maximum Health (only second to Azmodan), able to deal solid amount of burst damage and some good but avoidable poke damage during team fights while also having high waveclear for the laning phase. A well-placed Zombie Wall can be a lethal crowd control effect against many Heroes who do not have any Ability to counter it, especially if their allied Heroes have the same weakness.

abilities.title: Corpse Spiders
abilities.text: Hurl a jar of spiders that deals 50 (+4% per level) damage. If it hits at least one enemy, create 3 Corpse Spiders that attack for 38 (+4% per level) damage. Spiders last for 4 seconds. Corpse Spiders is a high-damage Ability that consists of a pot with Spiders inside it. Even if the pot deals damage too, the majority of the damage dealt by this Ability comes from the Spiders themselves. It is good to know that Spiders are immune to damage and will relentlessly attack the target enemy Hero for 4 seconds and eventually deny them from channeling an Objective for the duration.

abilities.title: Zombie Wall
abilities.text: After 1 second, create a ring of Zombies surrounding the target area that deal 28 (+4% per level) damage and last for 3 seconds. Zombie Wall is a powerful Ability that provides a unique form of crowd control by creating a circle of Zombies that block the path and attack nearby enemies at the same time, but it can either be dispersed with Knockback effects (such as Face Melt by E.T.C.), jumped over (for example with Dwarf Toss), or destroyed with damage (partially, by attacking a single Zombie, or completely, by damaging all of them with something like Blizzard). Although it is primarily used to immobilize enemy Heroes within the ring, allowing you and your allies to easily follow up with damage, it can also be used to completely block off narrow paths (for example the Gates between Towers), to tank the attacks of neutral Mercenaries (including Bosses), and to tank the shots from enemy Structures.

abilities.title: Plague of Toads
abilities.text: Recharge Time: 8 seconds Create a wave of 3 Toads that explode on contact, dealing 126 (+4% per level) damage over 6 seconds. This effect stacks. Stores up to 2 charges. Plague of Toads is a unique Ability that generates 3 Toads jumping in the chosen direction, each with a different angle. Toads are slow, therefore this Ability is mostly used to kill Minions and clear Mercenaries, to zone enemy Heroes that prefer not to take damage, or to safely poke enemy Heroes who are trying to channel an Objective. Sometimes you can also use it as a follow-up on allied crowd control, however, if you are too far from them, you will not hit the enemy Heroes in time regardless. Since all the Toads start from Nazeebo, a melee Hero (such as Thrall) will immediately take burst damage from all of them.

abilities.title: Gargantuan
abilities.text: Gargantuan (R) Nazeebo Heroic Summon a Gargantuan to guard an area, losing Health over 29 seconds. Deals 100 (+4% per level) damage when summoned, attacks for 140 (+4% per level) damage, and can be ordered to stomp nearby enemies. The Gargantuan's Stomp deals 240 (+4% per level) damage and Slows by 30% for 2 seconds. Gargantuan is a Summon that deals a significant amount of Spell Damage with Basic Attacks and can effectively zone low-Health or generally vulnerable Heroes out of a team fight by itself. You can use this Heroic Ability in various ways, from damaging enemy Heroes to tanking enemy Structures. Gargantuan Stomp is a very low cooldown Ability that can be used by Nazeebo to order Gargantuan to deal damage to enemy Heroes and Slow them.

abilities.title: Ravenous Spirit
abilities.text: Ravenous Spirit (R) Nazeebo Heroic Channel a Ravenous Spirit that deals 230 (+4% per level) damage per second. Cannot move while channeling. Lasts for 8 seconds. When you have Ravenous Spirit, always look for a safe position to cast it from. You do not necessarily have to hit multiple Heroes because getting a kill with a Heroic Ability is already a good trade. Zombie Wall can be used to block off a path before casting, preventing some Heroes from interrupting you.

abilities.title: Voodoo Ritual
abilities.text: Passive Nazeebo's Basic Attacks and Abilities poison Non-Heroic enemies, causing them to take 66 (+4% per level) additional damage over 6 seconds. Quest: If a Minion dies while poisoned by Voodoo Ritual, Nazeebo permanently gains 6 Health and 1 Mana. Voodoo Ritual is a Trait that causes Nazeebo's Basic Attacks and Abilities to deal damage over 6 seconds to non-Heroes hit. When clearing Minions, to maximize your damage output, you should try to quickly hit each of them at least once.

abilities.title: Baseline Quest
abilities.text: Nazeebo has a Baseline Quest which requires you to kill Minions affected by Voodoo Ritual. Whenever you do that, Nazeebo permanently gains 6 Health and 1 Mana, making him harder to kill in the late game. When playing as Nazeebo, you should try your best to make sure that all enemy Minions nearby are affected by Voodoo Ritual as they die. When playing with a Nazeebo in team, you should give Nazeebo enough time to debuff every Minion with Voodoo Ritual before killing them, otherwise he will not get stacks for his Baseline Quest.

opts.name: Widowmakers
opts.text: Enemies hit by Corpse Spiders' jar are Slowed by 25% for 1 second. Reward: After Corpse Spiders attack Heroes 100 times, their attack damage is increased by 25% and their duration is increased by 1 second.

opts.name: Pandemic
opts.text: Quest: Hit Heroes with Plague of Toads. Reward: After hitting 35 Heroes with Plague of Toads, it spawns 2 additional toads. Reward: After hitting 70 Heroes with Plague of Toads, it reduces the damage Heroes deal by 5%, stacking up to 25%.

opts.name: Thing of the Deep
opts.text: Increase the range of Nazeebo's Basic Abilities by 20%. Reward: After gaining 50 stacks of Voodoo Ritual, gain 5% Spell Power. Reward: After gaining 100 stacks of Voodoo Ritual, gain an additional 5% Spell Power.

opts.name: Hexed Crawlers
opts.text: Corpse Spiders restore 1% of Nazeebo's maximum Health and Mana when they attack an enemy Hero.

opts.name: Big Voodoo
opts.text: Increases the Health and Mana bonuses from Voodoo Ritual by 100%.

opts.name: Blood Ritual
opts.text: If an enemy dies while poisoned by Voodoo Ritual, restore 2% of Nazeebo's maximum Health and Mana. Passive: Takedowns grant 3 stacks of Voodoo Ritual.

opts.name: Spirit of Arachyr
opts.text: The number of Corpse Spiders spawned is increased from 3 to 4. If Corpse Spiders' jar hits only one enemy, it creates an additional spider.

opts.name: Dead Rush
opts.text: Zombie Wall deals 100% more damage. When it expires up to 5 remaining Zombies uproot and attack nearby enemies, losing Health over 3 seconds.

opts.name: Toads of Hugeness
opts.text: Increase the damage and explosion radius of Plague of Toads by 25% after each hop, up to a maximum of 100%.

opts.name: Gargantuan
opts.text: Mana: 90 Cooldown: 70 seconds Summon a Gargantuan to guard an area, losing Health over 29 seconds. Deals 100 (+4% per level) damage when summoned, attacks for 140 (+4% per level) damage, and can be ordered to stomp nearby enemies. The Gargantuan's Stomp deals 240 (+4% per level) damage and Slows by 30% for 2 seconds.

opts.name: Ravenous Spirit
opts.text: Mana: 100 Cooldown: 90 seconds Channel a Ravenous Spirit that deals 230 (+4% per level) damage per second. Cannot move while channeling. Lasts for 8 seconds.

opts.name: Guardian Toads
opts.text: Hitting an enemy Hero with Plague of Toads grants 30 Armor for 3 seconds, stacking up to 6 seconds.

opts.name: Superstition
opts.text: Gain 40 Spell Armor. Heroic Basic Attacks against Nazeebo remove this bonus for 3 seconds and spawn a Corpse Spider to attack the Hero.

opts.name: Ice Block
opts.text: Cooldown: 60 seconds Activate to place yourself in Stasis and gain Invulnerability for 3 seconds.

opts.name: Spider Colony
opts.text: Corpse Spider Attacks against Heroes reduce the cooldown of Nazeebo's Basic Abilities by 0.125 seconds.

opts.name: Ring of Poison
opts.text: Zombie Wall lasts 1 second longer, and the center is filled with poison that deals a total of 319 (+4% per level) damage over 4 seconds. This damage starts small and increases over the duration.

opts.name: Soul Harvest
opts.text: Cooldown: 15 seconds Activate to increase Nazeebo's Health and Spell Power by 7% for each nearby enemy, up to a maximum of 35%. Lasts 15 seconds.

opts.name: Humongoid
opts.text: Gargantuan Stomp's area is increased by 25% and its Slow amount is increased to 50%. Passive: Reduce Gargantuan's cooldown by 40 seconds and its Mana cost by 50%.

opts.name: Annihilating Spirit
opts.text: When Ravenous Spirit damages an enemy Hero, reduce their healing received by 50% for 1 second and increase Ravenous Spirit's damage by 5% for the rest of its duration. Passive: Increases the range of Ravenous Spirit by 50%.

opts.name: Vile Infection
opts.text: Quest: Reach 175 stacks of Voodoo Ritual. Reward: After reaching 175 stacks of Voodoo Ritual, it can also be applied to Heroes and its damage is increased from 66 (+4% per level) to 165 (+4% per level) over 6 seconds.

opts.name: Bad Medicine
opts.text: Cooldown: 30 seconds Consume 5 stacks of Voodoo Ritual to become Unstoppable, gain 20% increased Movement Speed, and 50 Armor for 2 seconds.

Nova.name: Nova
Nova.overview: Nova is a Ranged Assassin capable of using Stealth to confuse opponents and surprise them with ganks. Her strongest point is her exceptional long-ranged single-target burst damage. As a fragile Hero with no mobility tools, Nova needs to position safely and always have a retreat path ready.
strengths: Holo Decoy to counter some Abilities
Attack Range higher than most other Heroes
Good at ganking or just threatening so

build_notes.name: Holo Decoy Build
build_notes.text: Nova's Holo Decoy Build provides good single-target sustain damage from the mid game. Since you cannot choose the target of your Clones, this Build is more effective against partially or fully isolated enemy Heroes. Lethal Decoy at Level 16 increases your damage output when having Clones active, although you cannot choose who they will attack. Rapid Projection at Level 4 lets you do this more often and for less Mana. Ionic Force Field at Level 13 makes you and your Clones harder to kill. At Level 20, Rewind is the best option for burst damage, Precision Barrage provides more waveclear and area of effect damage, and Apollo Suit to confuse enemies with Stealth. Pinning Shot Build Advanced Nova's Pinning Shot Build provides superior single-target burst damage in the late game, also enabling allied Heroes to deal more damage if you all focus the same target. The combination of Double Tap at Level 13 and Crippling Shot at Level 16 is great for increasing not only your own damage but also your team's one.

build_notes.name: Snipe Build
build_notes.text: Nova's Snipe Build provides superior single-target sustain damage against Heroes in the early game and solid area-of-effect damage against Heroes and non-Heroes in the late game. Perfect Shot at Level 7 drastically increases your damage output, given you can constantly hit enemy Heroes with Snipe. Psionic Efficiency at Level 13 helps you to recover Precision Sniper stacks when you happen to miss enemies with Snipe. Explosive Round at Level 16 provides waveclear and can be used to hit targets that would be otherwise impossible to reach. Choose this Build when your team needs more waveclear, even though it comes online in the mid game, and when the enemy team features low-mobility Heroes that cannot easily dodge your Snipe.

build_notes.name: ARAM Build
build_notes.text: Nova's ARAM Build provides good single-target sustain damage from the mid game. Since you cannot choose the target of your Clones, this Build is more effective against partially or fully isolated enemy Heroes. Lethal Decoy at Level 16 increases your damage output when having Clones active, although you cannot choose who they will attack. Rapid Projection at Level 4 lets you do this more often and for less Mana. At Level 20, Rewind is the best option for burst damage, Precision Barrage provides more waveclear and area of effect damage, and Apollo Suit to confuse enemies with Stealth. See our Talents page for further information » Create your own build and share it with friends!

Nova.synergy_text: Nova works best with Heroes that provide one or many form of engage or crowd control, to help her deal damage with Snipe without the risk of missing too often. More importantly, Nova has to be paired with Heroes that make up for her huge lack of waveclear, otherwise your team will struggle doing anything during the game because of enemy Minions constantly giving vision to the enemy team and continually damaging your Structures until they fall.
Nova.counter_text: Being a Ranged Assassin with little in the way of escaping, Nova must rely on burst damage and long range to perform well. As a consequence, she struggles with anything that has tools for mitigating damage (for example Zarya) and against dive Heroes who get up close and personal with her (such as Zeratul). Nova does not like to play against global Heroes (notably Brightwing) because they can instantly nullify her numerical advantage when she is trying to gank someone. Never fully commit to a gank in those cases, otherwise it may backfire. Instead, play it safely and always be ready to retreat as someone else shows up.
Nova.maps_text: Nova's stronger maps Nova's average maps Nova's weaker maps Nova is a good choice on 2-lane Battlegrounds as they do not require a high amount of waveclear and they give her many opportunities to gank isolated enemy Heroes who tend to expose in the solo lane (such as Hanamura Temple). Due to her lack of waveclear, Nova is usually a bad choice on 3-lane Battlegrounds, especially if their Objective takes too long for her high Mana consumption to not be an issue (for example Alterac Pass) and/or requires to kill multiple Monsters at the same time (such as Infernal Shrines).
Nova.tips: If you fire Snipe when your target is between you and another enemy, a miss will probably hit the other target and thus not reset your Precision Sniper progress. Use Pinning Shot to make your Snipe and Precision Strike much easier to land. Holo Decoy is useful to intercept dangerous skillshots (such as Arcane Orb by Li-Ming) or to dismount enemy Heroes. While being easy to play around in team fights and near enemy Structures, Triple Tap is quite strong at taking down isolated enemy Heroes. Precision Strike can be used to globally clear Minion waves when needed, especially in side lanes with Catapults. See our Abilities page for further information »
Nova.meta_text: Nova, depending on the chosen Build, can either constantly pressure the enemy frontline with sustain damage or hit them with a big chunk of burst damage, with the help of allied Heroes capable of locking them down with crowd control effects. She is permanently Stealthed while out of combat, which makes tracking her position difficult as she will not appear on the enemy Minimap in those moments. Together with her solid damage output, this characteristic makes Nova good at ganking. The psychological pressure caused by a Nova pick is evident: while she is out of sight, opposing players tend to play more defensively, opening up windows of opportunities for your own teammates. She forces fragile Heroes to constantly have to consider their positioning in order to avoid her damage, which reduces their effectiveness. Due to not having mobility tools and being extremely weak to dive, Nova is not that popular in the current metagame, except when picked as a counter to peculiar Heroes who suffer the shenanigans she can perform with Holo Decoy (from blocking Hook by Stitches to defusing Steel Trap by Junkrat).

abilities.title: Snipe
abilities.text: Deal 230 (+4% per level) damage to the first enemy hit. Passive: Hitting an enemy Hero with Snipe permanently increases the damage of Snipe by 6%, stacking up to 30%. Gain an additional 25% damage bonus at maximum stacks. All stacks are lost if Snipe fails to hit an enemy. As Nova's main source of burst damage, Snipe is an essential Ability to master. Clever opponents will stand behind undesirable targets such as Minions, Summons, Structures, or resilient allied Heroes in order to prevent you from directly hitting them. They can also move in eccentric patterns or use mobility tools in an attempt to dodge the projectile. Crowd control effects that impair movement will help landing Snipe, but they are not available to Nova beside through Pinning Shot. Opponents that are distracted by certain tasks, such as killing Mercenaries or dealing with Objectives, are also significantly easier to hit. In the end, however, nothing makes up for being able to predict enemy movement and behavior, for which you will unquestionably need to practice. Learning to lead your target is a good first step to using Snipe well.

abilities.title: Pinning Shot
abilities.text: Deal 100 (+4% per level) damage to an enemy and Slow them by 40% for 2.25 seconds. Pinning Shot's unmissable nature and Slowing effect make it a part of a combo with Snipe and Precision Strike in order to improve your accuracy. The Ability's damage is so unremarkable that it should almost exclusively be used when the Slowing effect will be useful to you or a teammate, or to trigger One in the Chamber. Due to its long range and reliability, Pinning Shot is typically used as an opening Ability when ganking, allowing your allies to follow up with their own damaging or crowd controlling Abilities. As with most Slowing effects, it can also be used for peeling or hindering the escape of an opponent. It should be noted that Pinning Shot prompts Nova to automatically attempt to use a Basic Attack on the Ability's target if she is in range, unless ordered otherwise.

abilities.title: Holo Decoy
abilities.text: Create a Decoy for 5 seconds with 100% of Nova's current Health that attacks enemies, dealing 10% of Nova's base damage. Whenever a Decoy takes damage, it deals that amount of damage to itself, effectively doubling the damage it takes. Using this Ability does not break Stealth. Holo Decoy's usage varies widely based on your opponent's team composition. In general, placing the Decoy in a location where you could reasonably be, such as behind your team or in a bush, will make it difficult for your opponents to recognize which is the true Nova in order to attack you. In a best-case scenario, Abilities may be wasted against your Decoy instead of you or your teammates. The Decoy's attacks can also be used to force your opponents to dismount. Holo Decoy is also useful for scouting bushes, as its death is largely irrelevant beyond the used cooldown. Its puny damage can also be used to finish off opponents whom are out of the range of your other Abilities. Against Heroes with line skillshot Abilities (notably Hook by Stitches), Holo Decoy should almost exclusively be used to proactively prevent these Abilities from reaching you or your teammates. With enough experience and finesse, you can use Holo Decoy to reactively block these Abilities after you see them being cast. This has the advantage of making it impossible for your opponents to hold onto their Abilities for after your Decoy has vanished.

abilities.title: Triple Tap
abilities.text: Triple Tap (R) Nova Heroic Locks in on the target Hero, then fires 3 shots that hit the first Hero or Structure they come in contact with for 372 (+4% per level) damage each. Triple Tap's unmissable nature, extremely high damage, and long range make it a threat to any fragile or low-Health Hero. The slow movement of the projectiles fired by Triple Tap, on top of their very obvious travel pattern, means that clever opponents will move behind undesirable targets such as Structures or resilient allied Heroes in order to prevent you from hitting them. Coordinated teams make using Triple Tap even harder, as the projectiles are likely to be intercepted by the well-intentioned allies of your target. Most of these issues can be avoided by carefully selecting isolated targets that have no Structure or allies to use as cover. Being a stationary-channeled Ability, Triple Tap can easily be interrupted by various enemy crowd control effects, therefore its long range should be used to prevent this at all cost.

abilities.title: Precision Strike
abilities.text: Precision Strike (R) Nova Heroic After a 1.5 second delay, deals 435 (+4% per level) damage to enemies within an area. Unlimited range. Precision Strike is notable for its ability to deal a high amount of damage to any desired location of the battlefield. The 1.5-second impact delay means that it is prone to be avoided by attentive players. As such, Precision Strike is typically used with strong area of effect crowd control Abilities (such as Powerslide by E.T.C.). Casting Precision Strike on the escape path of a fleeing opponent may also force them to take the Ability's damage or momentarily stop their withdrawal. Precision Strike's global range also makes it useful for safely finishing off badly damaged Structures. Once you reach Level 13, you can start using Precision Strike for clearing distant Minion waves when needed because, thanks to scaling differences between Heroes and non-Heroes, it will one-shot Minions. To check exactly when that is possible, you can mouse-over Precision Strike to read its damage at a given Team Level (your scaling parameter) and use the Target Info Panel to see how much Health the enemy Footman Minions have at a given minute of Game Time (their scaling parameter). If you last-hit enemy Minions with it, in addition to helping that lane, you will get valuable Experience for your team.

abilities.title: Permanent Cloak
abilities.text: Gain Stealth when out of combat for 3 seconds. Taking damage, attacking, using Abilities, or Channeling ends Stealth. Remaining stationary for at least 1.5 seconds while Stealthed grants Invisible. Passive: Gain 15% Movement Speed while Stealthed. Permanent Cloak passively causes Nova to become Stealthed when out of combat for 3 seconds. Being Stealthed makes Nova untargetable by single-target Abilities and Basic Attacks, prevents Minions, Structures, and Mercenaries from engaging her, adds a large amount of transparency to her model, and prevents opponents from seeing her on the Minimap. Standing still for 1.5 seconds while Stealthed makes Nova completely Invisible until she moves. Permanent Cloak also increases Nova's Movement Speed by 15% while she is Stealthed. Stealth is lost when any of the following conditions is met: using a Basic Attack; taking damage; being hit by revealing Abilities; casting Abilities, including Talent-based Abilities such as Rewind, with the sole exception of Holo Decoy; channeling Objectives; summoning the Mount; using the Hearthstone; being near the opposing team's Fort, Keep, or Core. Permanent Cloak is a fundamental element of Nova's gameplay, allowing her to position herself to deliver her burst damage to the intended target. It is therefore essential that you learn the area of effect and cooldown of the Abilities that can reliably be used to break your Stealth. Common examples include Globe of Annihilation, Moonfire, Psionic Storm, and Multishot. It should be noted that the Stealthed state does not make Nova fully Invisible, though she can not be directly targeted or clicked. She instead appears to be transparent and heavily distorted, a visual effect often described as a shimmer. Attentive players can spot this shimmer and thwart your surprise attack attempts. It is generally best to assume that you are not Stealthed at all when dealing with opponents that are not distracted by some task. A new mechanic was recently introduced to allow you to achieve full Invisibility by standing still for 1.5 seconds. This is particularly useful for keeping an eye on Objectives or simply for setting up ganks.

abilities.title: Ghost Protocol
abilities.text: Activate to instantly grant Stealth to Nova and spawn a Holo Decoy at her location. Nova is Unrevealable for the first 0.5 seconds when Stealthed by Ghost Protocol. Ghost Protocol is Nova's only reliable defensive tool. It is generally used to escape melee Heroes who might have closed in on you, as its instant cast time allows you to benefit from Permanent Cloak's movement speed increase right as you need it. Furthermore, the Decoy summoned by Ghost Protocol can also be used to intercept skillshots such as Hook in a pinch. Under rare circumstances, Ghost Protocol can be used to get a little bit more damage out of the Decoy it summons, though this is rarely advisable unless necessary to secure a kill.

abilities.title: Baseline Quest
abilities.text: Nova has a Baseline Quest which requires to hit enemy Heroes with Snipe multiple times in a row without missing. There is no Reward for completing this Quest but each Snipe hit against Heroes increases the damage of subsequent Snipes. Failing to hit anything with Snipe sets this damage bonus back to 0, making it incredibly important to become a good sniper. Hitting non-Heroic enemies (such as Minions) does not reset these stacks, but will not provide more damage either. For this reason, it is always better to try and hit Heroes who are in front of other enemies as missing will at least result in a hit.

opts.name: Longshot
opts.text: Increases the cast range of Pinning Shot by 30%. Pinning Shot also increases the range of Nova's next Basic Attack by 2.3.

opts.name: Covert Ops
opts.text: After being Stealthed for 2 seconds, Pinning Shot's Slow is increased to 60% and costs no Mana. Bonus is lost after losing Stealth for 1 second.

opts.name: Advanced Cloaking
opts.text: After being Stealthed for 1 second, gain an additional 10% Movement Speed. While Stealthed, regenerate 6 Mana per second.

opts.name: Rapid Projection
opts.text: Reduces Holo Decoy's cooldown and Mana cost by 60%.

opts.name: Holo Stability
opts.text: Increase the cast range of Holo Decoy by 100% and its duration by 120%. Passive: Reduce the cooldown of Ghost Protocol by 15 seconds.

opts.name: Covert Mission
opts.text: Cooldown: 0.25 seconds Enemy Minions killed near Nova grant a stack of Bribe. Hero Takedowns grant 10 stacks of Bribe. Use 25 stacks to bribe a Mercenary, instantly defeating them. Does not work on Elite Mercenaries. Maximum of 100 stacks. If a camp is defeated entirely with Bribe, the camp respawns 50% faster.

opts.name: Perfect Shot
opts.text: Hitting an enemy with Snipe reduces its cooldown by 2 seconds and refunds half its Mana cost, doubled against enemy Heroes.

opts.name: One in the Chamber
opts.text: After using an Ability, Nova's next Basic Attack within 3 seconds deals 65% additional damage.

opts.name: Anti-Armor Shells
opts.text: Nova's Basic Attacks deal 250% damage and decrease the Physical Armor of Heroic targets by 15 for 4 seconds, but her Attack Speed is proportionally slower.

opts.name: Triple Tap
opts.text: Mana: 100 Cooldown: 100 seconds Locks in on the target Hero, then fires 3 shots that hit the first Hero or Structure they come in contact with for 372 (+4% per level) damage each.

opts.name: Precision Strike
opts.text: Mana: 100 Cooldown: 50 seconds After a 1.5 second delay, deals 435 (+4% per level) damage to enemies within an area. Unlimited range.

opts.name: Psionic Efficiency
opts.text: Snipe's range is increased by 15% and hitting a Hero grants an additional stack of Precision Sniper.

opts.name: Double Tap
opts.text: Pinning Shot now has 2 charges, but its cooldown is increased by 2 seconds.

opts.name: Ionic Force Field
opts.text: Gain 25 Armor for 3 seconds after losing Stealth.

opts.name: Explosive Round
opts.text: Snipe also deals 90% damage to enemies near the impact.

opts.name: Crippling Shot
opts.text: Pinning Shot lowers a Hero's Armor by 20 for the duration of the Slow, causing them to take 20% increased damage.

opts.name: Lethal Decoy
opts.text: Increases the damage Holo Decoy deals to 30% of Nova's damage.

opts.name: Fast Reload
opts.text: Triple Tap's cooldown is reset if it kills an enemy Hero.

opts.name: Precision Barrage
opts.text: Precision Strike gains a 2nd charge and its cooldown is reduced by 25 seconds.

opts.name: Apollo Suit
opts.text: Reduce the cooldown of Permanent Cloak by 2 seconds.

opts.name: Rewind
opts.text: Cooldown: 60 seconds Activate to reset the cooldowns of your Basic Abilities.

Orphea.name: Orphea
Orphea.overview: Orphea is an odd caster with above-average survivability and high damage output potential but limited access to crowd control. Given that all of Orphea's Abilities have a cast time or delay, they can all be avoided by prepared opponents... unless you are better prepared.
strengths: High sustain damage potential for a caster
weaknesses: All Abilities have a short cast time or delay, making them avoidable
Very limited access to crowd control
Relatively short range on most Abilities
Unable to efficiently claim Mercenary Camps
Easy to counter, as the main healing source can be countered by having blinds or physical armor
Particularly weak when playing from behind

build_notes.name: Standard Build
build_notes.text: This build is the most consistent build of them all, it can be used in any game, against any composition. The recommended Heroic is Eternal Feast, however, Crushing Jaws can also be picked to cancel a channeled ability, like Mosh Pit. At level 4 Allegrissimo can be chosen if the opposing team does not have any ways to quickly burst Orphea, and if she can consistently hit Shadow Waltz on a large target, like on Deathwing or Diablo. At Level 16 Lurking Terror can be chosen if Orphea's team needs better follow-up on a backliner, like on Hanzo or Valla.

build_notes.name: Shadow Waltz Build
build_notes.text: Orphea's Shadow Waltz Build focuses on improving sustain damage and chase potential. Even though this build has the highest possible DPS, it is challenging to make it work. Any crowd control greatly reduces Orphea's damage and survivability. Therefore, this build is only recommended for experienced players against compositions with low crowd control. Chomp Build Beginner Orphea's Chomp Build has the best survivability among all Builds, and it is the best for beginners, as its damage is not reliant on hitting Shadow Waltz or Dread. However, it is terrible against enemies with high range, as it requires proximity to them to be useful. This build has 2 main power spikes, the first one being on level 7, with Insatiable, which boosts Orphea's damage significantly. The second one is on level 13 with Abyssal Symbiosis, enhancing her survivability. After those levels, it is important to be take advantage of those strengths and focus on punishing enemies that are close to Orphea, as the extra shield and heal ensures that she will survive if not stunned or outnumbered.

build_notes.name: Aram Build
build_notes.text: Orphea's Aram Build is focused on high-range burst damage. To excel using this build, Orphea should focus on quickly completing her 2 quests, Growing Nightmare and Mind Devourer. Since Mind Devourer gets stacks from both the wave and explosion of Dread, it is always better to make sure that the wave will hit. Therefore, it is better to always aim Dread behind enemies. See our Talents page for further information » Create your own build and share it with friends!

Orphea.synergy_text: Since Orphea depends highly on skillshots to deal damage, she works well with any Hero that can provide reliable crowd control. Her frailty also makes her dependent on other Heroes to peel for her against melee Assassins particularly; Tanks tend to fulfill these two needs, though other Hero types can too.
Orphea.counter_text: Since Orphea relies heavily on skillshots with a cast time to deal damage and on hitting her charged Basic Attacks to heal herself, she is countered by many heroes. Her damage and survivability can be significantly reduced by canceling her abilities, blinding or evading her basic attacks, dashing out of her abilities, chaining crowd control, or using very high range attacks.
Orphea.maps_text: Orphea's stronger maps Orphea's average maps Orphea's weaker maps Orphea is a strong pick on snowball maps. She excels on maps with important bosses, like Sky Temple and Tomb of the Spider Queen, because her Eternal Feast is excellent in these situations. However, her lack of single-target PvE damage makes her a poor choice on maps like Battlefield of Eternity. As long as another hero can claim Mercenary Camps, she remains a reasonable pick on most maps.
Orphea.tips: Each enemy Hero hit by Overflowing Chaos generates one Chaos, making area hits key to improving your survivability. Shadow Waltz may be tempting to use on-Cooldown, but using it to avoid dangerous skillshots is paramount. Shadow Waltz does not require Orphea to instantly dash after hitting an enemy, the dash can be used after a delay to avoid a skillshot or to wait for her next ability to be ready. Shadow Waltz's dash can be used to dodge certain player created walls, such as Leoric's Entomb or Tassadar's Force Wall. Chomp synergises naturally with Shadow Waltz; use the latter to dash to your intended target. Both Dread's initial wave and eruption can hit a given target, so it is better to aim slightly behind an immobilized or slowed target. Before having Dead Magic, it is better to not waste Orphea's empowered Basic Attack on an armored enemy, as it would greatly reduce her healing output. After reaching Level 20 with Crushing Jaws and picking Engulfing Oblivion, Orphea should not hesitate to use it on a tank enemy, as the -50 armor debuff is enough to burst anyone down. See our Abilities page for further information »
Orphea.meta_text: Compared to most other casters, Orphea provides higher-than-average on-demand burst damage and decent sustain damage. On the other hand, she lacks much crowd control, making it necessary to pick her along Heroes who can provide it. As with many Heroes who provide little more than damage, Orphea's popularity depends entirely on her power level resulting from game balance. Regardless, building a team composition that aims to stay ahead of one's opponents in terms of Experience is the best way of exploiting Orphea's strength as a snowballing Hero. Due to her reliance on crowd control, Orphea is at her best when part of a roaming group of Heroes. She can hold her own in the offlane as well against most melee Heroes, but must be careful when rotating and may need help clearing out large Mercenary Camps.

abilities.title: Shadow Waltz
abilities.text: After 0.5 seconds, deal 165 (+4% per level) damage to enemies in a line. Hitting a Hero with Shadow Waltz sets its cooldown to 2 seconds, refunds 35 Mana, and causes Orphea to dash a short distance upon moving. Shadow Waltz is Orphea's most important Ability. Shadow Waltz's short Cooldown (2 seconds on Hero hits) gives it a high sustain damage output, especially when considering Overflowing Chaos. Shadow Waltz's cooldown, however, is significantly higher when failing to hit an enemy Hero (5 seconds). This makes accuracy and the ability to follow up on crowd control important skills for Orphea players to develop. Shadow Waltz's name comes from the short dashing effect that follows a successful hit. This dashing effect can be triggered by right-clicking a point or unit, upon which Orphea will rapidly move a short distance towards the target. This effect can and should be used, as possible, to avoid enemy skillshots or otherwise reposition yourself offensively for Basic Attacks or Chomp. It should be noted that while Orphea can dash through units, she cannot dash through terrain and Structures. However, she can move through some walls generated by certain Heroes, such as Leoric's Entomb or Tassadar's Force Wall. Further, she cannot dash while under the effects of movement-preventing crowd control. Since Shadow Waltz has a 0.5 seconds cast time, care is required so as to not miss one's intended target. In parallel, enemies are likely to try and avoid Shadow Waltz due to its importance to Orphea, making mindgames an important aspect of the Hero. Although using Shadow Waltz on-Cooldown may be tempting, its utility in avoiding dangerous Abilities makes restrained use much more prudent under most circumstances.

abilities.title: Chomp
abilities.text: After 0.625 seconds, deal 305 (+4% per level) damage to nearby enemies in front of Orphea. Chomp is Orphea's highest damage Ability. Its very short range and relatively long cast time, however, make it difficult to use on its own. This is why it is generally preceded by an offensive Shadow Waltz's dash to close the gap between Orphea and the intended target. This combo is, in fact, the crux of Orphea's offensive playstyle, particularly when following up allied crowd control. Chomp's area of effect is large enough to allow it to hit an entire Minion wave, although its short range makes retaliation easy for opponents. In fact, one should always be very mindful of their surroundings when using Chomp at any time.

abilities.title: Dread
abilities.text: Release a wave of dread that deals 85 (+4% per level) damage to enemies hit. Dread erupts 0.75 seconds after reaching the end of its path, dealing 175 (+4% per level) damage. Enemies hit by Dread's wave or eruption are Slowed by 25% for 2 seconds. Dread is Orphea's filler Ability. Its long range allows it to be lobbed at immobile enemy Heroes and Minions alike safely and to good effect. Since Dread's eruption effect has a short delay, it can be avoided by opponents. As such, you should see to aim slightly ahead so as to force them to take the hit or fall back and risk being hit by your other Abilities. It should be noted that both Dread's initial wave and eruption can hit a given target, making it optimal to aim slightly behind immobile targets (such as those under the effects of crowd control) so as to ensure double hits. Further, Dread's eruption's Slow effect can help with hitting Shadow Waltz and Chomp alike, as well as provide a limited means of self-peeling.

abilities.title: Eternal Feast
abilities.text: Eternal Feast (R) Orphea Heroic After 1.5 seconds, deal 210 (+4% per level) damage in an area. Eternal Feast repeats every 1 second as long as it hits an enemy Hero. Eternal Feast is a large area of effect Ability designed specifically for area denial. In other words, its purpose is to force enemies away from a specific area of effect for fear that they may repeatedly trigger Eternal Feast. Due to its long 1.5-second initial delay, hitting enemies with Eternal Feast without the help of crowd control is unlikely. Without allied crowd control to setup for it, Eternal Feast is generally used to break team fights apart or on important points of contention such as Objectives and Bosses.

abilities.title: Crushing Jaws
abilities.text: Crushing Jaws (R) Orphea Heroic After 1.25 seconds, pull enemies in an area towards the center, dealing 250 (+4% per level) damage and Stunning them for 0.5 seconds. Crushing Jaws is Orphea's main team fighting Ability and only true source of crowd control. Successful Crushing Jaws hits allow you to follow up with each of your other Abilities perfectly for significant amounts of damage. Your allies, too, may find Crushing Jaws' effects useful to secure their own hits. As such, you should aim to hit two or more Heroes, as possible. Beware, however, as Crushing Jaws has a delay of 1.25 seconds, making it easy to avoid for Heroes with a gap closer that is off-Cooldown. Crushing Jaws should certainly be used in conjunction with allied crowd control so as to prevent it from being avoided. Crushing Jaws also opens up the possibility for Orphea to land solo kills against some of the squishier Heroes, assuming it is followed up with your other Abilities. Since Crushing Jaws has a relatively short cooldown, this should be done whenever possible if you think you can secure a kill.

abilities.title: Overflowing Chaos
abilities.text: Passive Hitting an enemy Hero with a Basic Ability grants 1 Chaos. Chaos can stack up to 3 times. While Orphea has Chaos, her Basic Attacks against Heroes consume all Chaos, dealing 50% increased damage per stack, and healing for 100% of the damage dealt. Overflowing Chaos is Orphea's source of self sustain, and represents a good reason to use Basic Attacks as often as possible, unlike most casters. To maximise the use of Overflowing Chaos, one Basic Attack should be used against a Hero every time 3 stacks are reached, as further stacks provide no additional effect. Shadow Waltz can be used to help deal such Basic Attacks and generally quickly generate Overflowing Chaos stacks. It should be noted that hitting multiple Heroes with a single Basic Ability cast does generate multiple Overflowing Chaos stacks, making area hits desirable to try and land.

opts.name: En Pointe
opts.text: Shadow Waltz deals an increased 90% damage to enemies hit by its end and grants 1 additional Chaos.

opts.name: Growing Nightmare
opts.text: Increase Dread's damage by 50%. Quest: Hit 3 enemy Heroes with a single cast of Dread's eruption. Reward: Permanently increase Dread's eruption damage by 50% and increase the Slow amount of Dread's eruption by 15%.

opts.name: Ancestral Strength
opts.text: Non-Heroic Abilities deal 15% more damage to Stunned, Rooted, Silenced or Slowed enemies. Enemy Heroes who are hit with Overflowing Chaos are Slowed by 20% for 2.5 seconds.

opts.name: Allegrissimo
opts.text: Reduce the cooldown of Shadow Waltz by 1 second. Hitting Heroes with the end of Shadow Waltz sets its cooldown to 0.75 seconds.

opts.name: Backbiter
opts.text: If Chomp hits a Hero, Orphea immediately dashes a short distance backwards. Passive: Gain 15% maximum Health.

opts.name: Chaotic Assault
opts.text: Basic Attacks against enemy Heroes while having 3 stacks of Chaos deal an additional 75% bonus damage.

opts.name: Insatiable
opts.text: Hitting a Hero with Chomp sets its cooldown to 2 seconds.

opts.name: Ravenous Hunger
opts.text: Quest: Minions that die within 1.5 seconds of being hit by Chomp permanently increase its damage by 2 and heal Orphea for 60 (+4% per level). Heroes that die increase its damage by 40 and heal Orphea for 25% of her maximum Health.

opts.name: Mind Devourer
opts.text: Quest: Hitting Heroes with Dread increases its damage by 5, up to 150. Reward: After hitting 30 Heroes, hitting an enemy Hero with Dread's eruption sets its cooldown to 6 seconds and refunds 50 Mana.

opts.name: Eternal Feast
opts.text: Mana: 75 Cooldown: 50 seconds After 1.5 seconds, deal 210 (+4% per level) damage in an area. Eternal Feast repeats every 1 second as long as it hits an enemy Hero.

opts.name: Crushing Jaws
opts.text: Mana: 75 Cooldown: 70 seconds After 1.25 seconds, pull enemies in an area towards the center, dealing 250 (+4% per level) damage and Stunning them for 0.5 seconds.

opts.name: Determination
opts.text: After dashing with Shadow Waltz, Orphea gains 50 Spell Armor against the next enemy Ability, stacking up to 2 times. While Orphea has Determination, her Physical damage is increased by 15%.

opts.name: Abyssal Symbiosis
opts.text: Hitting a Hero with Chomp instantly grants Orphea maximum Chaos and a 170 (+4% per level) Shield for 3 seconds.

opts.name: Invasive Miasma
opts.text: Cooldown: 10 seconds Activate to deal 150 (+4% per level) damage to all nearby enemies after 2 seconds. For each Hero hit, heal for 182 (+4% per level) and gain 1 Chaos.

opts.name: Bond of Anguish
opts.text: Shadow Waltz deals bonus damage to Heroes equal to 3% of their maximum Health, healing Orphea for 50% of damage dealt.

opts.name: Dead Magic
opts.text: Basic Attacks that consume Chaos ignore Armor and deal 90 (+4% per level) Spell Damage to the target and all enemies around them.

opts.name: Lurking Terror
opts.text: Mana: 60 Cooldown: 10 seconds After Dread erupts and for 2 seconds after, activate to cast Chomp from the eruption area. Enemy Heroes hit by this Chomp are Slowed by 70% for 1.5 seconds.

opts.name: Monster Within
opts.text: Eternal Feast grants 1 Chaos each time it hits a Hero. While Eternal Feast is active and for 5 seconds afterwards, Orphea's Basic Abilities recharge 150% faster.

opts.name: Engulfing Oblivion
opts.text: Crushing Jaws reduces the Armor of Heroes hit by 50 for 3 seconds. Takedowns set its cooldown to 5 seconds.

opts.name: Eldritch Conduit
opts.text: Each Chaos consumed increases Orphea's Spell Power by 3%, up to 30%. After reaching the maximum bonus, the Spell Power is increased by an additional 30%. Lasts 10 seconds.

opts.name: Final Toccata
opts.text: Cooldown: 20 seconds Activate to instantly reset the cooldown of Shadow Waltz. For the next 5 seconds, dashing with Shadow Waltz resets its cooldown and increases the duration of Final Toccata by 1 second.

pairs.text: Leoric Orphea Leoric can use Entomb to block enemy Heroes in place for multiple seconds and Orphea can follow-up with Eternal Feast to damage them while they cannot move out of its area. Note that some Heroes can get out of Entomb by using teleports or some dashes that can go over impassable terrain, and Anduin can counter this combo with Leap of Faith.

Probius.name: Probius
Probius.overview: Probius is a Ranged Assassin who excels at zone control by means of setting up and activating a plethora of structures and abilities. When given the opportunity, Probius is able to craft a devastating gauntlet that will cripple the entire enemy team. His bread and butter ability combo ( Disruption Pulse/ Warp Rift) can deal massive amounts of AoE damage to multiple enemies, while Photon Cannon will chip away at any and all who stray too close. At Level 10, Probius is able to chose between damage ( Pylon Overcharge) and utility ( Null Gate), either of which will greatly aid his allies in combat.
strengths: Good area of effect burst damage
Great staying power, impressive Mana regen via Warp In Pylon
Able to contest Objectives for a long duration
weaknesses: No reliable hard crowd-control like stuns or roots

build_notes.name: Photon Cannon Build
build_notes.text: Photon Cannon's Build is a balanced Probius build that focuses on always having several Photon Cannons active in the battlefield. Echo Pulse is picked instead of Gather Minerals because of its synergy with his Level 7 Talent, Tower Defense. It is important to always use Photon Cannons and Disruption Pulse when they are available, as Probius can get a whole cooldown refund in a single Disruption Pulse with these Talents. See our Talents page for further information » Create your own build and share it with friends!

Probius.synergy_text: Probius works best with Heroes that provide a strong frontline he is able to seek refuge behind, as well as supports who can assist in peeling away enemies attempting to dive him. These Heroes also should have some reliable source of hard crowd-control since Probius unfortunately does not have any himself until Level 10 with Null Gate.
Probius.counter_text: Probius is countered by high mobility Assassins with large amounts of burst damage and crowd-control. Probius' lack of a gap-closer may regularly be capitalized on by more agile opponents.
Probius.maps_text: Probius's stronger maps Probius's average maps Probius's weaker maps Probius performs best on larger Battlegrounds that revolve heavily around objectives that he is able to have ample time to set up for. Probius has incredible staying power and is able to easily prevent enemies from capturing certain objectives (such as Altars on Towers of Doom) with his ranged abilities and Photon Cannons. Battlegrounds with lots of narrow spaces and chokepoints give Probius many places to hide Pylons and force enemy Heroes through the effected area of his Warp Rifts.
Probius.tips: Unlike mounts, Worker Rush may be used in combat. Keep in mind that ALL damage (including damage-over-time such as poisons) will immediately break the effect. Place Pylons from Warp In Pylon within brush or behind terrain or allied fortification to protect them from being immediately destroyed. Do not be afraid to poke enemies with Disruption Pulse when unable to set up or waiting on the cooldown of Warp Rift. Warp Rift is most effective when used in narrow corridors and chokepoints that force enemies to travel through its AoE. Photon Cannon is great for zoning as well as soaking damage from Minions, Mercenaries, and enemy structures. Save Pylon Overcharge for teamfights surrounding important Battleground objectives. This will force the enemy to either stay within its range or give up the objective to disengage, either of which are good for Probius and his allies.
