opts.name: Demoralizing Shout
opts.text: Cooldown: 20 seconds Activate to demoralize nearby enemy Heroes, reducing damage they deal by 40% for 5 seconds. Each time an enemy Hero affected by Demoralizing Shout deals damage to a Hero, reduce its cooldown and Parry's cooldown by 5%.

Whitemane.name: Whitemane
Whitemane.overview: Whitemane is a Healer who can heal her allies with Zeal by damaging her enemies. She is capable of trading damage favourably against most Heroes, and must do so in order to maximise her healing. If she is able to consistently deal damage, she can generate immense healing for her team.
weaknesses: Very poor waveclear and Camp clear
Healing output largely dependent on damage dealt, therefore low out-of-combat healing

build_notes.name: Inquisition Build
build_notes.text: Whitemane's Inquisition Build is based on Talents that increase the defensive and offensive effectiveness of Inquisition, making it a useful peeling tool and a powerful follow up for allied engages. Subjugation at Level 13 will reduce the damage done by enemy Heroes and Shared Punishment at Level 16 will reduce their Armor, a great combination of Talents that will shift damage and healing in your team's favor. To do all of this more often, we have Pity the Frail at Level 1. Searing Lash Build Advanced Whitemane's Searing Lash Build empowers Searing Lash, increasing your damage output and giving you access to crowd control in the late game. Consider going for this Build when you expect Inquisition to be interrupted too often and too quickly. Block enemy Heroes with Harsh Discipline at Level 16 to help your team deal more damage to them or to peel when needed. When doing so, you can easily get a cooldown reset from Lashing Out at Level 13.

build_notes.name: ARAM Build
build_notes.text: Whitemane's ARAM Build is based on Talents that increase the defensive and offensive effectiveness of Inquisition, making it a useful peeling tool and a powerful follow up for allied engages. Subjugation at Level 13 will reduce the damage done by enemy Heroes and Shared Punishment at Level 16 will reduce their Armor, a great combination of Talents that will shift damage and healing in your team's favor. To do all of this more often, we have Pity the Frail at Level 1. See our Talents page for further information » Create your own build and share it with friends!

Whitemane.synergy_text: Whitemane has synergy with Heroes who can create a lot of space (for example Johanna) or that like to take prolonged team fights (such as Sonya) as she can keep healing them for long. Due to the high amount of raw healing she has access to, Whitemane is great when paired with Heroes who have Armor baseline (like Garrosh) or with high uptime (notably Cassia).
Whitemane.counter_text: Whitemane has very limited mobility, and must remain within the threat range of enemies in order to deal damage to heal her allies. She will struggle against Heroes who can displace her, as she lacks any kind of escape once caught, or crowd control her to death. Heroes who can deal damage to Whitemane and her teammates while she cannot damage them back (for example Chromie) may be difficult to play against. Additionally, Heroes who can significantly reduce or prevent healing received (such as Deckard Cain with Sapphire at Level 7) can greatly reduce the effectiveness of Zeal during teamfights.
Whitemane.maps_text: Whitemane's stronger maps Whitemane's average maps Whitemane's weaker maps Whitemane excels in short team fights and at contesting Objectives that take less than 30 seconds to be secured (for example Infernal Shrines). If the fight takes too long, she struggles to keep up with her Mana consumption. The least interesting Maps to play Whitemane on are the ones where she cannot abuse her kit around the Objective, that are heavily focused on Mercenaries (such as Sky Temple), or where the early game is too important (notably Braxis Holdout).
Whitemane.tips: Desperate Plea is the only Ability in Whitemane's kit that has a Mana cost, but you have to manage your Mana wisely because of the Desperation mechanic. Use Inquisition immediately after casting Searing Lash to maximise your damage output while they are Slowed. Cast Searing Lash when you can hit enemy Heroes, preferably when they are under crowd control effects that impair their movements. Scarlet Aegis can be used during team fights to apply Zeal to multiple allied Heroes without having to pay Desperation cost, given they are in range. Divine Reckoning should be preferably used as a follow-up to allied crowd control effects that can keep enemy Heroes in place. Make sure to apply Zeal to allied Heroes before using your Abilities to deal damage, otherwise you will not convert that damage into healing. When there are no enemy Heroes in range, make sure to use Clemency to sustain your team with out-of-combat healing. To save Mana, try to use either Inquisition or Clemency to remove 1 Desperation stack before casting Desperate Plea again. See our Abilities page for further information »
Whitemane.meta_text: Whitemane excels at relatively quick team fights, during which she can get value from her burst healing and have time to go back for restoring her Mana. Among her Talents, she has various tools to save teammates from enemy Heroes who hard engage, leading the opponents to expose for getting a kill and then suddenly deny it. Whitemane needs to be able to deal damage in order to heal optimally, so a strong frontline is necessary for her to reach peak performance. Her complete lack of waveclear is another weakness that will limit the team compositions she can fit into. She must have allies who can generate enough map pressure to make up for her weak macro. Although Whitemane has clearly defined weaknesses, she can be powerful in many team compositions, given they have a strong frontline and plenty of waveclear.

abilities.title: Desperate Plea
abilities.text: Heal an allied Hero for 140 (+4% per level) and gain Desperation for 4 seconds. Desperation increases Desperate Plea's Mana cost by 40, and stacks up to 3 times. Current Mana Cost: 45 Desperate Plea is the only Ability in Whitemane's kit that has a Mana cost. It is also the only Ability in her kit that has no cooldown. While it does provide a small amount of direct healing, the primary function of Desperate Plea is to apply Zeal to allies relatively often. The Desperation mechanic allows you to decide on your own cooldown. Casting Desperate Plea often with full Desperation stacks is not sustainable. You should generally prioritise allies that need Zeal during early fights. A good thing to remember is that the Zeal buff lasts longer than the Desperation debuff. This means that with careful management, Zeal can be sustainably applied to several allies at once. A good practice to default to is to cast Desperate Plea twice, and then wait for Desperation to expire before casting it again. While there will be many situations that require you to improvise outside of this pattern, it is a good starting point to preserve your Mana for when you need it. In case of emergency, do not hesitate to use Desperate Plea several times in a row, regardless of how many Desperation stacks you have. This way you can save an allied Hero from death at the cost of having to use your Healing Fountain or your Hearthstone to get Mana before the next team fight, which does not give Experience to the enemy team and is faster than waiting for an allied Hero to respawn in the late game.

abilities.title: Inquisition
abilities.text: Channel on an enemy Hero for up to 3 seconds, dealing 50 (+4% per level) damage every 0.5 seconds and Slowing them by 30%. Removes a stack of Desperation. Shares a cooldown with Clemency. Inquisition damages a target enemy Hero, but must be channeled. This means that it will lock Whitemane in place unless it is cancelled or interrupted. You should choose wisely when to start casting this Ability so you can keep channeling it for longer but you should also not hesitate cancelling it to move in case of danger or to cast another Ability if needed. Because Inquisition removes 1 stack of Desperation, Desperate Plea should ideally be cast at least once just before channeling it. This way, you can damage someone and then reapply Zeal by spending less Mana. Inquisition may also be used specifically for the Slow effect. If an enemy Hero is out of position and your Allies are nearby, reducing their Movement Speed may help your team secure a kill. Inquisition has a rather long cooldown, and should be used this way only when allies are likely to complete the takedown. Inquisition should be primarily used to maximise your healing output when allies need it.

abilities.title: Searing Lash
abilities.text: After 0.5 seconds, smite enemies in a straight line for 82 (+4% per level) damage. If the first strike hits an enemy Hero, a second strike will occur after a short delay. Repeatable Quest: Hit Heroes with Searing Lash. Repeatable Quest: Hit 3 Heroes with Basic Attacks. Reward: Permanently increase Whitemane's maximum Health by 3 and Mana by 2. Heroes hit with the second strike of Searing Lash count as 2 hits. Searing Lash has a low cooldown, no Mana cost, and a very short cast animation. It should usually be cast whenever it is available. It is good to practice casting it all the time, as this will increase your familiarity with the Ability. Once constant use of Searing Lash is second nature, it will be easier to do while managing Desperate Plea's Desperation stacks. Searing Lash should ideally be on cooldown right before casting Inquisition because its cooldown will keep going while you are busy channeling that.

abilities.title: Scarlet Aegis
abilities.text: Scarlet Aegis (R) Whitemane Heroic Bolster the spirits of nearby allied Heroes, healing them for 300 (+4% per level) and granting them 40 Armor for 4 seconds. Scarlet Aegis is a fantastic Heroic that heals all nearby allies, which applies Zeal to them. This means that you can apply Zeal to all teammates simultaneously without gaining any Desperation stacks. The armor provided by this Heroic is also very beneficial.

abilities.title: Divine Reckoning
abilities.text: Divine Reckoning (R) Whitemane Heroic After 1 second, consecrate an area for 4 seconds, dealing 50 (+4% per level) damage every 0.5 seconds to enemies inside. 25% of the damage dealt to Heroes is returned as Mana. Divine Reckoning deals damage over time in an area. This can be a great way to increase your healing through Zeal. Divine Reckoning works best in team compositions that can help trap enemies inside the consecrated area.

abilities.title: Zeal
abilities.text: Whitemane's healing Abilities apply Zeal for 8 seconds. Allies with Zeal are healed for 100% of the damage Whitemane deals to Heroes. Activate to gain 25% Spell Power and lose 15 Armor for 5 seconds. Can be cast while channeling abilities. Zeal is an extremely powerful buff that can be applied to Whitemane and her allies. By converting damage into healing, it allows Whitemane to trade damage exceptionally well and to heal several members of her team at the same time. Whitemane's damage-dealing Abilities can and should be thought of as potential healing, multiplied by the number of allied Heroes with a Zeal buff on them. Because of this, it is important to think about how to maximise your damage per second when playing her. This can be accomplished by casting her damage dealing Abilities as often as it is safe to do so. When the enemy team commits to a fight, it is ideal to have Zeal applied to all allied Heroes who are in combat. Zeal can be applied to teammates with any healing Whitemane provides that is not from Zeal itself. This means that Desperate Plea, Clemency, and Scarlet Aegis can be used to apply Zeal. Understanding this is important for Mana management because Desperate Plea is the only tool Whitemane has that has any Mana cost limiting its use. Zeal's active component temporarily increases Whitemane's Spell Power and reduces her Armor. This can greatly increase Whitemane's healing and damage done with Abilities for a short time but will also increase Whitemane's vulnerability to damage taken, so you should activate it only when not in danger.

abilities.title: Clemency
abilities.text: Activate to cast Inquisition on an allied Hero, healing them for up to 329 (+4% per level) over 3 seconds while Channeling. Removes a stack of Desperation Shares a cooldown with Inquisition. Clemency heals a target allied Hero, but must be channeled. This means that it will lock Whitemane in place unless it is cancelled or interrupted. You should choose wisely when to start casting this Ability so you can keep channeling it for longer but you should also not hesitate to cancel it to move in case of danger or to cast another Ability if needed. Because Clemency removes 1 stack of Desperation, Desperate Plea should ideally be cast at least once just before channeling it. This way, you can heal someone and then reapply Zeal by spending less Mana.

abilities.title: Baseline Quest
abilities.text: Whitemane has a Baseline Quest which requires to hit enemy Heroes with Searing Lash. Every hit increases your maximum Health by 3 and maximum Mana by 2. You should not play too much around this Baseline Quest because Whitemane is perfectly playable without additional Health and Mana. That said, any additional Health and Mana you gain is good for you.

opts.name: Pity the Frail
opts.text: For every Hero hit with Searing Lash, lower the cooldown of Inquisition by 1 seconds. Allies below 30% Health receive 25% more healing from Whitemane.

opts.name: Righteous Flame
opts.text: Searing Lash deals 25% more damage to enemies. If the second strike hits an enemy Hero, they take an additional 25% damage and Whitemane gains 40% Attack Speed for 3 seconds.

opts.name: Inquisitor's Prayer
opts.text: Searing Lash restores 25 Mana for each Hero it hits, and Zeal lasts 2 additional seconds.

opts.name: Unwavering Faith
opts.text: Increase Whitemane's Basic Attack range by 1.1. Whitemane gains 20% increased Basic Attack damage for each active Zeal buff.

opts.name: Martyrdom
opts.text: Desperate Plea's healing is increased by 30%. Increase this by an additional 10% for each active Zeal.

opts.name: Indulgence
opts.text: Gain 5% Movement Speed. Increase this by an additional 5% for each active Zeal.

opts.name: Zealous Spirit
opts.text: Upon reaching 2 stacks of Desperation, Whitemane gains Zeal.

opts.name: Saintly Greatstaff
opts.text: Enemy Heroes hit by Searing Lash are marked for 3 seconds. Basic Attacks against them deal an additional 55 (+4% per level) Spell damage and remove the mark.

opts.name: Intercession
opts.text: Cooldown: 75 seconds Activate to make an ally Unstoppable for 1 second.

opts.name: Scarlet Aegis
opts.text: Cooldown: 60 seconds Bolster the spirits of nearby allied Heroes, healing them for 300 (+4% per level) and granting them 40 Armor for 4 seconds.

opts.name: Divine Reckoning
opts.text: Cooldown: 75 seconds After 1 second, consecrate an area for 4 seconds, dealing 50 (+4% per level) damage every 0.5 seconds to enemies inside. 25% of the damage dealt to Heroes is returned as Mana.

opts.name: Subjugation
opts.text: Inquisition reduces all damage the target deals by 50%.

opts.name: Lashing Out
opts.text: If Searing Lash's second strike hits an enemy Hero, reduce its cooldown to 1 second.

opts.name: Scarlet Wrath
opts.text: Basic Attacks against Heroes increase the duration of all active Zeals by 0.75 seconds, restore 1% Mana to all Zeal targets, and lower the cooldown of Zeals activation by 4 seconds.

opts.name: Radiance
opts.text: Reaching 3 stacks of Desperation heals for 190 (+4% per level) and reapplies Zeal to allies with Zeal.

opts.name: Shared Punishment
opts.text: Upon casting, Inquisition can chain to an additional enemy Hero near its target, dealing 50 (+4% per level) damage every 0.5 seconds. Affected enemies lose 10 Armor.

opts.name: Harsh Discipline
opts.text: Hitting a Hero with Searing Lash while they are being targeted by Inquisition Roots them for 1.5 seconds. Passive: Reduce Inquisition's cooldown by 2 seconds.

opts.name: Scarlet Crusade
opts.text: Scarlet Aegis heals for 50% more and makes affected allies Unstoppable for 2 seconds.

opts.name: Judgment Day
opts.text: Divine Reckoning deals 50% more damage and pulls enemies to its center the first time it hits them.

opts.name: Guiding Light
opts.text: Cooldown: 30 seconds Activate to cast a permanent Zeal on an allied Hero that costs no Mana and doesn't grant Desperation. Only one can be active at a time and has global cast range. Increases the Spell Power bonus provided by Whitemane's trait by 15%.

opts.name: Purge the Wicked
opts.text: Cooldown: 40 seconds Activate to blast an enemy Hero with holy fire, reducing their Armor by 25 and dealing 300 (+4% per level) damage over 4 seconds.

Xal'atath.name: Xal'atath
Xal'atath.overview: Xal'atath is a Ranged Assassin who can deal burst damage by hitting an enemy Hero with the center of Shadow Mark and detonating Dark Heart Ritual on them. Unlike many mages, she can Basic Attack while moving. Her attacks deal substantial Physical Damage even to frontline Heroes and charge Void Volley, so she can keep dealing damage between Ability casts. Xal'atath is very fragile and has only Void Step to escape. Its long, telegraphed teleport sequence gives enemies time to react, while she must keep using Basic Attacks to charge Void Volley. Although she is difficult to play safely, her mix of good Physical Damage from Basic Attacks and burst damage from Void Volley and her other Abilities is hard for enemies to mitigate, making her rewarding when played well.
strengths: Has great area of effect damage
Can stall channeled Objectives with Dark Heart Ritual
weaknesses: Burst depends on landing delayed skillshots

build_notes.name: Dark Heart Ritual Build
build_notes.text: The Dark Heart Ritual Build controls space, especially at narrow choke points. Dark Heart Ritual should be placed across paths enemies must take to advance or retreat, forcing them to take damage and, with Pull of the Dark Heart, be Slowed. This Build is also strong on Maps with channeled Objectives, such as Cursed Hollow and Towers of Doom. With Anchored Core, the Dark Heart lasts 10 seconds and Dark Heart Ritual has a 15-second cooldown. By placing it on the Objective every 15 seconds, Xal'atath can stall its 6-second channel on her own indefinitely, as long as she stays in range and can keep casting.

build_notes.name: Void Volley Build
build_notes.text: The Void Volley Build maximizes Xal'atath's burst damage and adds utility through Dark Heart's Protection's Silence. It works best with allied crowd control, which helps stack Void Adept and Void Volley. Keep Basic Attacking anything in range to charge Void Volley, then use it to hit enemy Heroes whenever possible. Reaching its first 20 Quest stacks is essential for this Build. If your Tank has reliable crowd control, spend the early game using only Basic Attacks and Void Volley until they catch an enemy Hero. Then follow up with Shadow Mark and Dark Heart Ritual to detonate the Dark Heart on the Marked target. Without reliable allied setup, use Dark Heart Ritual on enemy Heroes or Minion waves, then aim Shadow Mark at Heroes leaving its area. In small skirmishes, try Shadow Mark first. If you miss, wait 2 seconds before placing Dark Heart Ritual on the wave. Shadow Mark will be ready roughly 4 seconds later; hitting a Hero with its center lets the previously placed Dark Heart pursue and detonate on them for a Void Adept stack while you clear the wave. Void Step Build Not recommended The Void Step Build requires Xal'atath to use Void Step aggressively in fights to deal damage. Spending her only mobility Ability to close in leaves her vulnerable to Stuns. Even if enemies cannot stop her, they can leave Basic Attack range between blinks, making the damage from Relentless Whispers inconsistent. For these reasons, we do not recommend this Build.

build_notes.name: ARAM Build
build_notes.text: The ARAM Build focuses on Shadow Mark and stacking Void Adept. To get the most out of the Quest, hold Dark Heart Ritual until Shadow Mark hits an enemy Hero, then cast it to detonate the Dark Heart on the Marked target. ARAM's frequent fights let Xal'atath stack Void Adept quickly, so she can already deal substantial burst damage by Level 7 with Toxic Mark. See our Talents page for further information » Create your own build and share it with friends!

Xal'atath.synergy_text: Allied crowd control gives Xal'atath a window to land Shadow Mark's center and several Void Volley projectiles. It also gives the Dark Heart time to reach a Marked target. Void Prison and Containment Disc let Xal'atath charge Void Eruption in advance.
Xal'atath.counter_text: Shadow Mark travels slowly, and Void Volley's projectiles launch over time, giving mobile enemies a chance to avoid both. Xal'atath has low Health, little self-peel, and only Void Step to escape. Hard engages such as Dragon's Arrow or Leap can catch her before she can reposition, especially if she has already used Void Step.
Xal'atath.maps_text: Xal'atath's stronger maps Xal'atath's average maps Xal'atath's weaker maps Xal'atath benefits from Maps that bring teams together for frequent fights. They give her more chances to stack Void Volley, while narrow areas make her area-of-effect skillshots easier to land. Infernal Shrines, Volskaya Foundry, and Towers of Doom have contested spaces that make Dark Heart Ritual and Shadow Mark harder to avoid. She struggles on Maps where enemies can flank from several directions. Her low Health and predictable Void Step make it hard to escape once surrounded.
Xal'atath.tips: Anchored Core lets Dark Heart Ritual repeatedly deny 6-second Objective channels. With Unstable Core at Level 20, its flames cover the rest of the 15-second cooldown, allowing continuous denial of even 3-second channels if you cast Dark Heart Ritual on time and stay in range. Activate Void Step while a Basic Attack is already traveling toward an enemy to give that attack the first 10% damage bonus when it lands. With Void Acolyte, cast a charged Void Volley before Void Step, then fire the free, 25%-stronger Volley after Void Step ends. Hit ranged Minions with Shadow Mark before placing Dark Heart Ritual in the wave. This helps the Dark Heart get the last hits so you can leave without collecting Experience Globes. When escaping with Void Step, reactivate it as soon as you reach a safe position. Ending the teleport sequence early lets you move again sooner. With Void Acolyte, complete Void Step at the Hall of Storms before heading back to a lane. The free Void Volley remains available as long as you do not Basic Attack an enemy. If Void Volley is charged before a rotation, cast it at an enemy Hero or a nearby Tower just before mounting. The charge would otherwise expire, and Void Volley deals excellent siege damage. See our Abilities page for further information »
Xal'atath.meta_text: In the early game, Xal'atath should clear waves while working toward Void Volley's first 20 Quest stacks. Stay near your Tank until reaching that milestone, since dying before it loses all Void Volley stacks. At 20 stacks, Void Volley gains range, making enemy Heroes easier to hit and giving Xal'atath more freedom to follow allied crowd control or look for a gank. Dying now costs at most 6 stacks without removing the milestone. From Level 7, following that crowd control with Shadow Mark's center also applies Toxic Mark's Armor reduction, greatly increasing the team's burst damage. The extra range does not protect you from flanks. If enemies are hunting you, keep Void Step ready to escape instead of spending it to follow an engage, and let your Tank peel when they turn on you.

abilities.title: Shadow Mark
abilities.text: Shoot a Void Orb that deals 60 (+4% per level) damage to enemies hit, and an additional 120 (+4% per level) damage to enemies in the center. If an enemy Hero or Structure is hit by the center, they are marked for 4 seconds. Targets afflicted by Shadow Mark are Revealed and draw the Dark Heart and Void Minions towards them. Shadow Mark fires an Orb that damages enemies it hits, dealing extra damage at its center. Every enemy Hero or Structure hit by the center is Marked and Revealed for 4 seconds. Cold Feet at Level 4 and Toxic Mark at Level 7 can each extend the Mark by 1 second, up to 6 seconds with both Talents. Marked targets remain Revealed for the Mark's duration. Any Dark Heart or Void Minions already active, or summoned while the Mark is active, are directed towards the Marked target. If the Mark expires before they reach it, they continue moving towards that target. The most reliable way to land Shadow Mark's center is to wait for allied crowd control before casting it. Without that setup, you can place Dark Heart Ritual to make an enemy move away from the Dark Heart, then aim Shadow Mark along their expected path. You can also queue Void Step away from the enemy immediately after casting Shadow Mark. The blink hides the Orb's initial animation, making it appear to fly from Xal'atath's new position and giving the enemy less time to react. Queue Dark Heart Ritual before Shadow Mark as well to set up a quick detonation on the Marked target after blinking away.

abilities.title: Dark Heart Ritual
abilities.text: Summon the Dark Heart, which pulses for 50 (+4% per level) damage per second to nearby enemies and lasts 8 seconds. The Dark Heart moves to Shadow Mark's impact location. The Dark Heart will pursue targets afflicted by Shadow Mark and detonate on impact, dealing 245 (+4% per level) damage to nearby enemies and 61 (+4% per level) more damage to the Marked target. Dark Heart Ritual summons the Dark Heart for 8 seconds, damaging nearby enemies once per second. While the Heart is active, casting Shadow Mark sends it to the Orb's impact location, even if the Orb does not Mark anyone. If no target is Marked, the Heart continues moving until it reaches that location. If an enemy is Marked before or after the Heart is summoned, it pursues that target. The Heart detonates on contact only if the enemy is still Marked, damaging nearby enemies and dealing additional damage to the Marked target. The Dark Heart pulses once when summoned and once each second afterward, for 9 pulses over its 8-second duration. Anchored Core extends its duration by 2 seconds, allowing 2 more pulses. To get the most damage from it, let it pulse for as long as possible before detonating it on a Marked target near the end of its duration. For waveclear, place the Dark Heart in the middle of the enemy wave as soon as possible, since its damage takes time to be dealt. Hit the ranged Minions with Shadow Mark before summoning the Dark Heart. The Orb softens them for the Heart to finish without moving it. When the Heart gets the last hit, you gain Experience immediately, so you can mount and leave without needing to collect Experience Globes from the Ranged Minions. If you hit the melee Minions with Shadow Mark instead, they may die first, allowing your Minions to advance and last-hit the ranged Minions. Those kills leave Experience Globes that you need to collect before leaving, slowing your rotation speed. Place the Dark Heart over a channel point to repeatedly interrupt attempts to capture Objectives such as Tributes on Cursed Hollow or Seeds on Garden of Terror. With Anchored Core at Level 1, its longer duration can repeatedly deny 6-second channels and make 5-second channels difficult to complete if you keep the Dark Heart on the Objective and cast it whenever it is ready. Enemies can still finish 3-second channels in the gap between casts.

abilities.title: Void Step
abilities.text: Cast to teleport Xal'atath 3 times in a triangular pattern. Each time Xal'atath teleports, her Basic Attacks deal 10% more damage while the Ability is active. Reactivate to end Void Step early and remain at your current location. Void Step teleports Xal'atath three times, moving counterclockwise around the points of a triangle. Each teleport increases her Basic Attack damage by 10% while Void Step is active, up to 30%. Reactivate it to end the sequence early at her current position. Void Step is Xal'atath's only way to escape, and its predictable path gives enemies time to react. Keep it ready when you might need to retreat, and reactivate it once you reach a safe position so you can move again sooner.

abilities.title: Void Volley
abilities.text: After attacking enemies with her Basic Attacks 5 times, Xal'atath can activate Void Volley to unleash a barrage of 6 Void Orbs at a target location, each dealing 90 (+4% per level) damage on impact. Charge fully decays if Xal’atath does not hit an enemy with a Basic Attack after 6 seconds. Quest: Hit enemy Heroes with Void Volley to grant 1 stack per hit and increases Void Volley's damage by 1%. Lose all stacks upon dying. Reward (20 Stacks): +2 Void Volley Range Stack loss on death lowered to 6. Reward (60 Stacks): -1 Basic Attack required to charge Void Volley. Mythic Reward (100 Stacks): +50% Basic Attack and Void Volley Damage. Void Volley projectiles Pierce all targets. Stack loss will never cause the Hero to fall below a quest reward threshold. After five Basic Attacks against enemies, Xal'atath can cast Void Volley to fire six Orbs at a location. A charge obtained through Basic Attacks expires after 6 seconds unless Xal'atath hits an enemy with another Basic Attack. Each Orb that hits an enemy Hero adds a Quest stack and increases Void Volley's damage. At 20 stacks, it gains range and loses fewer stacks on death. At 60, it needs one fewer Basic Attack to charge. At 100, its projectiles pierce and both Basic Attacks and Void Volley gain damage.

abilities.title: Void Eruption
abilities.text: Heroic Channel a powerful Void Orb that grows over time until reaching maximum size after 2 seconds. Recast to launch the Orb early. Enemies that come into contact with the Orb take 112 (+4% per level) damage and are Blinded for 1 second. When the Orb reaches the end of its path, it detonates in a large explosion, dealing 400 (+4% per level) damage. Charging up this Ability increases its contact damage up to 175 (+4% per level) and its explosion damage up to 700 (+4% per level). Contact damage is dealt every 0.25 seconds. Void Eruption channels a growing Orb. Enemies who touch it take periodic damage and are Blinded. Recast to launch the Orb early. It explodes at the end of its path, and charging it longer increases both its contact and explosion damage.

abilities.title: Void Convergence
abilities.text: Heroic After channeling for 2 seconds, summon a Void Portal that spawns up to 3 Void Minions to attack nearby enemies. You can have up to 1 active Void Portal. Enemies near the Void Portal are Slowed by 25%. Void Minions are attracted to targets afflicted by Shadow Mark. The Portal expires after 20 seconds. Void Minions automatically choose a nearby lane to push. Void Minion Basic Attacks deal 50 (+4% per level) damage per hit. Void Minions lose Health over 12 seconds. Void Convergence channels for 2 seconds before summoning a Void Portal that lasts up to 20 seconds if not attacked. The Portal Slows nearby enemies and spawns up to three Void Minions, which follow targets Marked by Shadow Mark or move into a lane. Only one Portal can be active at a time.

opts.name: Void Adept
opts.text: Quest: Detonate the Dark Heart on targets afflicted by Shadow Mark. Each successful detonation permanently increases Shadow Mark and the Dark Heart Ritual Detonation damage by 20, up to 10 times.

opts.text: Activating Void Step grants 50% Movement Speed and 25 Spell Armor for 2 seconds. This bonus refreshes each time Xal'atath teleports.

opts.name: Dark Barrier
opts.text: Each time Dark Heart damages an enemy, Xal'atath gains a Shield equal to 2% of her maximum Health, up to 10%.

opts.name: Void Acolyte
opts.text: Completing Void Step fully charges Void Volley. The next Void Volley deals 25% increased damage and costs no Mana.

opts.name: Toxic Mark
opts.text: +1s Shadow Mark Duration Heroes affliced with Shadow Mark have their Armor reduced by 10 and take damage equal to 1% of their maximum Health every second.

opts.name: Silence of the Lamb
opts.text: Activating Void Step summons a seal of void magic on the ground. When the seal completes, it deals 250 (+4% per level) damage to enemies inside and Silences them for 1 seconds.

opts.name: Void Summoner
opts.text: Activating Void Step summons a single Void Minion in Xalatath's original postion. Void Minions are attracted to targets afflicted by Shadow Mark. Void Minions automatically choose a nearby lane to push. Void Minion Basic Attacks deal 50 (+4% per level) damage per hit. Void Minion loses Health over 12 seconds.

opts.name: Void Eruption
opts.text: Mana: 80 Cooldown: 75 seconds Channel a powerful Void Orb that grows over time until reaching maximum size after 2 seconds. Recast to launch the Orb early. Enemies that come into contact with the Orb take 112 (+4% per level) damage and are Blinded for 1 second. When the Orb reaches the end of its path, it detonates in a large explosion, dealing 400 (+4% per level) damage. Charging up this Ability increases its contact damage up to 175 (+4% per level) and its explosion damage up to 700 (+4% per level). Contact damage is dealt every 0.25 seconds.

Enemies near the Void Portal are Slowed by 25%. Void Minions are attracted to targets afflicted by Shadow Mark. The Portal expires after 20 seconds. Void Minions automatically choose a nearby lane to push. Void Minion Basic Attacks deal 50 (+4% per level) damage per hit. Void Minions lose Health over 12 seconds.

opts.name: Pull of the Dark Heart
opts.text: Enemies damaged by the Dark Heart Ritual are Slowed by 10% for each pulse, stacking up to 5 times and decaying over 1 seconds.

opts.name: Dark Heart's Protection
opts.text: Casting Dark Heart Ritual Silences enemies inside its radius for 1 second. Xal'atath and allied Heroes gain 30 Spell Armor while inside the Dark Heart's radius.

opts.name: Crushing Cascade
opts.text: Enemies hit by Void Volley are Slowed by 6% for 1 seconds per projectile, up to 50%.

opts.name: Marked Resilience
opts.text: Basic Attacks against enemy Heroes afflicted by Shadow Mark grant a 160 (+4% per level) point Shield that rapidly decays. Shield starts decaying after 1 second, decays over 2 seconds.

opts.name: Relentless Whispers
opts.text: While Void Step is active, Xal'atath's Basic Attack Speed is increased by 150%.

opts.name: Fractured Reality
opts.text: +25% Void Volley Projectile Damage Void Volley's projectiles leave behind a trail of fire for 3 seconds, constantly dealing 9 (+4% per level) damage to enemies. Damage is increased the longer a target stands in the flames. Damage is dealt every 0.1875 seconds. Damage increases up to 300%. Damage increase from multiple fires stack.

opts.name: Harbinger's Consumption
opts.text: Void Eruption splits into 3 orbiting Void Orbs. Each enemy Hero hit by their explosions reduces Void Eruption's cooldown by 14 seconds.

opts.name: Rift Invasion
opts.text: Void Convergence's Void Portal no longer has a life duration, raises the active Void Portal limit to 2, and can spawn and sustain up to 4 Void Minions.

opts.name: Dueling Orbs
opts.text: +1 Shadow Mark Charge Shadow Mark has a 3 second cooldown between uses.

opts.name: Unstable Core
opts.text: When the Dark Heart expires or detonates on a target afflicted by Shadow Mark, it leaves behind a pool of void flames for 5 seconds. Enemies in the flames take 45 (+4% per level) damage over time. The flames deal damage every 1 second.

opts.name: Paradox Loop
opts.text: After completing Void Step, Xal'atath immediately performs a second Void Step in the opposite direction. Added effects are triggered again. Bonus Basic Attack damage stacks up to 3 times

Xul.name: Xul
Xul.overview: Xul is a high damage Bruiser that abuses his strong AoE damage from his abilities to quickly clear any minion wave, which then allows him to create many Skeletal Warriors thanks to Raise Skeleton, letting him become a major threat to towers and, by extension, making the wave much harder to clear. Xul also excels against melee compositions, given he can easily land Cursed Strikes into many targets, reducing their attack speed and making him really hard to deal without crowd control.
strengths: Decent self-sustain thanks to Bone Armor and Harvest Vitality
Good crowd control for team to follow up thanks to Bone Prison
Able to apply lots of debuffs on attack speed, damage, healing and armor
weaknesses: Weak against compositions featuring many ranged or poke-centric heroes
Really hard to play when facing counters

build_notes.name: Scythe Build
build_notes.text: The Scythe Build offers plenty of AoE damage thanks to the additional Scythes offered by Echoes of Death at Level 13. Due to Mortal Wound at Level 20, this build becomes particularly powerful against double Healer composition who rely on a lot of healing. Unfortunately The Scythe Build is very dependent on Decrepify, which comes a bit too late and might not be a good choice if your team is looking for early-game fights.

build_notes.name: Cursed Strikes Build
build_notes.text: Xul's Cursed Strikes Build gives Xul much survivability thanks to Harvest Vitality's sustain, while Weaken provides considerable resistance by reducing enemy damage dealt. Since this build requires you to be constantly hitting many enemies with Cursed Strikes, it excels against melee-heavy compositions with little crowd control. This build is the most effective at capturing or clearing Mercenaries, considering Xul will have Cursed Strikes up nearly all the time, with very high Attack Speed. Backlash can be replaced with Shade when facing many Basic Attacks-reliant Heroes, like Raynor or Illidan. Both Poison Nova and Skeletal Mages are useful, though it is recommended to go with Poison Nova when facing many melee Heroes. Skeletal Mages will perform well when you need some kind of crowd control to reach the targets you are looking for.

build_notes.name: Bone Prison Build
build_notes.text: Xul's Bone Prison Build has much more burst than the other options. It is a great choice if the opposing team has lots of crowd control, ranged Heroes, or burst damage, since you will not be able to get much value out of Cursed Strikes. Backlash can be replaced with Shade when facing many Basic Attack-reliant Heroes, like Raynor, Illidan, or Greymane. If you are having trouble facing the opposing laner, we recommend changing both the Level 4 and 7 Talents into Grim Scythe and Harvest Vitality respectively, since they will give you much more self-sustain while clearing waves, without crippling your burst capabilities. See our Talents page for further information » Create your own build and share it with friends!

Xul.synergy_text: Xul sinergizes very well with Heroes that are able to protect him while he receives burst damage or crowd control like Medivh. He also excels with good follow up for Bone Prison, like Tyrande with Lunar Flare, Falstad with Hinterland Blast or Li-Ming with all her Abilities.
Xul.counter_text: Due to not having mobility, Xul suffers a lot from displacement effects or crowd control in general, making Heroes such as E.T.C. huge threats, while Johanna is able to Blind him during Cursed Strikes, reducing his effectiveness. Xul also struggles against Heroes with long range or with high burst damage that allows them to follow up the crowd control, like Jaina and Sgt. Hammer.
Xul.maps_text: Xul's stronger maps Xul's average maps Xul's weaker maps Xul shines in maps with nearby lanes, as he will be able to easily abuse his waveclear and Skeletal Warriors, making him excellent on Blackheart's Bay, Tomb of the Spider Queen, and Infernal Shrines. He will also be decent on big maps where the Objective will be very time consuming, allowing him to get a great experience lead through split-pushing, like in Sky Temple, Garden of Terror, or Cursed Hollow. However, Xul does not perform as well in 2-lane maps, given he cannot abuse his fast waveclear to spawn skeletons and go to another lane, which he normally would in a bigger map.
Xul.tips: Cursed Strikes is one of the best waveclear Abilities in the game, so you should always be attempting to clear a wave and instantly Mount up and rotate to another lane, getting maximum value out of Raise Skeleton. Since Xul does not have a strong early game, sometimes it is better to (in some maps) avoid fighting for the first Objective (Infernal Shrines and Cursed Hollow can be good examples), and instead proceed to the opposite lane in order to split-push between the other 2 lanes. A good practice is to warn your team before doing this, given they will be having a numerical disadvantage in the fight, and will have to play it safe. Keep in mind Xul has limited mobility, so during fights it is a good idea to wait for your tank to engage, or for enemy heroes to spend their crowd control before going in, given you will struggle to enter and escape fights. A good way to use Bone Prison is on a tank just after they spent their defensive skills, a Johanna without Iron Skin or an Anub'arak without Burrow Charge often turn out to be an easy kill, given they will be rooted in the same place for 2 seconds. Since Bone Prison has a tiny range, it is recommended to always stay mounted so you can easily find a way to engage your desired target. See our Abilities page for further information »
Xul.meta_text: Each minion wave spawns every 30 seconds (starting from 00:00); this has the same cooldown as Bone Armor, which allows you to ignore the enemy Bruiser every time you step up to clear the wave. Thanks to this, Xul will always be ahead of his enemies, enabling him to move towards the closest lane to either gank or clear it. Since Xul is slightly dependent on talents to be really impactful in fights, it is better to focus on clearing waves between two lanes during the early game. After you get your main talent for the build ( Harvest Vitality for Cursed Strikes Build, Amplify Damage for Bone Prison Build, and Decrepify for Spectral Scythe Build) start looking for fights, Xul will be extremely good in them.

abilities.title: Raise Skeleton
abilities.text: When a nearby enemy Minion dies, it becomes a Skeletal Warrior with 240 (+4% per level) Health that attacks for 21 (+4% per level) damage and lasts up to 12 seconds. Upon death, Skeletal Warriors deal 40 (+4% per level) damage to nearby enemies. Up to 3 Skeletal Warriors can be active at once when spawned in this way. Xul's trait will not only increase his pushing capabilities greatly, but will also greatly increase his damage in fights. Up to 3 Skeletal Warriors can be active at once, and every extra Summon evoked will make the first spawned to explode dealing 40 damage to enemies, allowing you to deal decent damage into the opposing laner by just hitting the wave. If the enemy is far from your warriors, you can use Bone Prison to make skeletons move towards them to guarantee the explosion damage while clearing the other Minions.

abilities.title: Bone Armor
abilities.text: Activate to gain a Shield equal to 25% of Xul's maximum Health for 3 seconds. Bone Armor can help Xul a lot when facing opposing laner, since he can use it to ignore the damage received while clearing the wave. This is a recommended tactic when you are having trouble rotating faster, but be aware that the Shield is your main way to survive ganks. Only use it in the wave if you are sure that you will not get ganked soon. After getting Harvest Vitality, Xul will have a lot of self-healing in fights. It is better to only use Bone Armor when you are below 70% Health to not lose value from healing. If the opposing team features a lot of crowd control or burst damage, the Shield should be used early on to prevent you from dying during a Stun or Silence. Bone Armor will be a whole different skill depending of Xul's Level 1 Talent. The differences and how it should be used will be mentioned in the Talent Build page.

abilities.title: Spectral Scythe
abilities.text: Summon a scythe that travels to Xul after 1 second, dealing 190 (+4% per level) damage to enemies and spawning a Skeletal Warrior when hitting enemy Heroes. These do not count towards Xul's Raise Skeleton maximum. Spectral Scythe causes Xul to summon a scythe to the target location that travels back to him after 1 second, dealing a large amount of damage to all enemies in its path. Xul's waveclear becomes even more powerful if he uses Spectral Scythe effectively, which usually requires him to place the scythse behind enemy Archer Minions. Aiming and landing Spectral Scythe can sometimes be tricky, especially against moving enemy targets. Consequently, it is often recommended to wait until you have successfully Rooted someone by using Bone Prison and then following up with Spectral Scythe on the imprisoned target. After getting Mortal Wound at 20, it is recommended to only use against someone with low life or affected by some crowd control, considering the healing reduction will be much more useful than the damage.

abilities.title: Cursed Strikes
abilities.text: Passive Xul's Basic Attacks deal damage in a wide area and reduce the Attack Speed of Heroes and Summons by 40% for 2 seconds. Lasts 4 seconds once triggered. Cursed Strikes will make all your attacks for the next 4 seconds cleave. 5 attacks can be landed in the duration, so it is crucial to hit all of them. If your enemy starts running from you after you activate it, keep walking towards them while stopping to attack the closest Minion or Hero every time you can, so your cleave will hit them even when they are outside of your Attack range. During team fights, Cursed Strikes should be used against Attack Speed dependent Heroes, such as Illidan, Thrall, or Kharazim, in order to cripple their combat efficiency. When getting ganked, Xul can deny a considerable part of the damage by landing some Cursed Strikes attacks while walking backwards, reducing their Attack Speed.

abilities.title: Bone Prison
abilities.text: After a 2 second delay, deal 80 (+4% per level) damage and Root the target enemy Hero for 1.75 seconds. All nearby Skeletal Warriors will fixate on the target for their duration. Bone Prison is an incredibly powerful crowd control Ability for two major reasons. Firstly, its 2-second Root effect provides enough time for Xul and the rest of his team to approach the affected enemy target and damage it. Secondly, Bone Prison comes with flashy visual effect that marks the chosen enemy, which clearly signalises your allies which target to focus while it also causes all of your active Skeletons to fixate on the Rooted target for additional damage. A good way to use Bone Prison is on a Tank just after they spent their defensive skills. Johanna without Iron Skin or an Anub'arak without Burrow Charge often turn out to be an easy kill, given they will be Rooted in the same place for 2 seconds.

abilities.title: Poison Nova
abilities.text: Poison Nova (R) Xul Heroic After 0.5 seconds, release poisonous missiles that deal 630 (+4% per level) damage to all enemies hit over 10 seconds. Poison Nova is an incredibly strong Heroic Ability that deals almost half the life of a Hanzo or a Valla. However, that damage will be dealt over 10 seconds, thus allowing Healers to easily save the dying target. It is also easy to avoid when you are not close to Xul. Therefore, Poison Nova is a really good option when either facing a composition with many melee Heroes, or against Healers incapable of supporting all their team, as they only have single-target healing (such as Lt. Morales). Using Poison Nova right at the start of a fight might not be a good idea, since it will be easily dodged by the ranged opposing Heroes. It is recommended to wait a couple seconds after fight starts to use it, complicating for enemy Heroes without mobility tools (for example Kael'thas) to dodge it, as they might be focused on other things in the combat.

abilities.title: Skeletal Mages
abilities.text: Skeletal Mages (R) Xul Heroic Summon 4 Frost Mages in a line that attack nearby enemies for 47 (+4% per level) damage a second and Slow them by 30% for 2 seconds. Last up to 15 seconds. Skeletal Mages is a great tool to zone enemy Heroes and Slow them down. The efficiency of Skeletal Mages can be increased even further if your team has decent crowd control Abilities, which enable you to follow up extremely well on targets already Slowed by Skeletal Mages. Skeletal Mages is a crucial Heroic Ability when you are having trouble getting close to ranged Heroes, as the Slow will enable you to reach them. Due to the relatively long cooldown on Skeletal Mages, it should be cast with caution. Use narrow choke points and impassable terrain to your advantage in order to successfully trap enemy high-priority targets.

Yrel.name: Yrel
Yrel.overview: Yrel is a resistant Bruiser who excels at creating opportunities to decide fights in her team's favor. Since all of her Basic Abilities come with a short wind-up time, it is extremely important to think ahead when playing Yrel in order to avoid getting interrupted or missing the right moment to strike.

build_notes.name: Vindication Build
build_notes.text: Yrel's Vindication Build provides a good balance of survivability, damage, and utility. While playing this Build, you should generally use Divine Purpose right before casting Vindication. Righteous Hammer Build Advanced Yrel's Righteous Hammer Build provides a good balance of survivability, damage, and utility. While playing this Build, you should generally use Divine Purpose right before casting Righteous Hammer.

build_notes.name: Avenging Wrath Build
build_notes.text: Yrel's Avenging Wrath Build provides a good balance of survivability, damage, and utility. While playing this Build, you should generally use Divine Purpose right before casting Avenging Wrath.

build_notes.name: ARAM Build
build_notes.text: Yrel's ARAM Build provides a good balance of survivability, damage, and utility. While playing this Build, you should generally use Divine Purpose right before casting Vindication. See our Talents page for further information » Create your own build and share it with friends!

Yrel.synergy_text: Yrel can help Tanks with a weak engage to force a fight by finding a good flank and can support the ones who lack peeling to protect the backline from aggressive enemy Heroes. The Armor from Aegis of Light at Level 4 is great for protecting allied Heroes who lack mobility. Garrosh benefits from it more than other Heroes because it stacks with Armor Up. The healing from Gift of the Naaru at Level 4 can be useful for playing in the offlane as a 2-man with Zarya on Braxis Holdout. This strategy allows you to have good damage and survivability on both lanes. The ability to provide Movement Speed and remove some crowd control effects with Hand of Freedom at Level 4, together with the possibility to use Righteous Hammer defensively when needed, is quite useful for helping allied Heroes who are in trouble.
Yrel.counter_text: Yrel suffers against Heroes that possess reliable crowd control effects who can interrupt her Basic Abilities as they are being channeled (Stuns and Silences) or who can interrupt Avenging Wrath during its jump animation (Roots and Knockbacks). She also struggles against Heroes who can kite her from the distance or have a lot of mobility to deal damage without being hit in return. While laning, these Heroes could threaten a gank, forcing Yrel to use her Heroic Ability to stay alive. Last but not the least, Yrel is relatively weak to healing reduction effects (especially if having Ardent Defender as Heroic Ability), Armor reduction effects (especially if having Sacred Ground as Heroic Ability), and percent-based damage because they all reduce her survivability during team fights.
Yrel.maps_text: Yrel's stronger maps Yrel's average maps Yrel's weaker maps Thanks to her excellent waveclear, Yrel does better on Maps where she can double soak. After gaining priority over the enemy Offlaner, she can rotate to force a fight with a numerical advantage over the enemy team. When contesting a Capture Point, Yrel can make use of her survivability to buy time and rely on Righteous Hammer to Knock enemy Heroes away. This is not only useful for securing Mercenary Camps but also for controlling some Objectives. Yrel can unleash her true potential on Maps where there are various spots to flank by manually charging up Avenging Wrath while hidden, jump over impassable terrain to close the distance, and still have Divine Purpose to instantly fully-charge Righteous Hammer.
Yrel.tips: Vindication should be used on cooldown while laning, even if not hitting anyone, because it is your main source of self-sustain. Combine it with Divine Purpose to save Mana. Righteous Hammer can be used either aggressively, to engage for punishing enemy Heroes, or defensively, to peel for allied Heroes in need of help. Avenging Wrath is best used to engage by channeling it behind impassable terrain, to take enemy Heroes off-guard. Divine Purpose should be used when you need to fully charge a Basic Ability. The specific Basic Ability to fully charge this way depends on your Build and sometimes even on the situation. Ardent Defender should ideally be used when Yrel is around 50% maximum Health instead of waiting until the last moment. This way you can keep fighting instead of having to retreat anyway. Sacred Ground is best used to secure a Capture Point but can also be used to mitigate burst damage when needed during team fights. Hand of Freedom can be used not only to remove Roots and Slows from Yrel or an allied Hero, but also to simply give them Movement Speed when needed. Seraphim is great for becoming Unstoppable while channeling a Basic Ability, so that you cannot get interrupted. See our Abilities page for further information »
Yrel.meta_text: Yrel is an amazing Offlaner that can easily fight the enemy in her lane and roam before them, flanking enemies with Avenging Wrath to push them towards your team with Righteous Hammer. While laning, she is not that easy to gank and her self-sustain allows her to perform well even in unfavorable match-ups. During team fights, Yrel excels at flanking the enemy team and peeling for allied Heroes in need. Thanks to her self-sustain, Yrel does well against sustain damage. After reaching Level 10, Yrel can get away with playing very aggressively when her Heroic Ability is not on cooldown as they can mitigate a lot of burst damage when active.

abilities.title: Vindication
abilities.text: Unleash holy energy around Yrel, dealing 48 (+4% per level) damage to nearby enemies and healing her for 111 (+4% per level). Charging up this Ability increases its damage up to 160 (+4% per level), and healing up to 370 (+4% per level). Vindication is a Basic Ability which heals Yrel and deals damage to all enemies around her. As you channel it, it deals more healing and damage. As for all Yrel's Basic Abilities, you can activate Divine Purpose right before casting Vindication to instantly cast it as if you fully charged it up. When doing so, it costs no Mana and cannot be interrupted before going off. While laning, you can use this Ability for waveclear, for damaging enemy Heroes, and also for self-sustain while not fighting. This last part is quite important to stay healthy in lane because, when playing as an Offlaner, you will often have no Healer nearby.

abilities.title: Righteous Hammer
abilities.text: Swing Yrel's hammer, dealing 42 (+4% per level) damage to enemies in front of her and knocking them away. Charging up this Ability increases its knockback distance, and damage up to 140 (+4% per level). Enemies hit at maximum charge are Stunned for 1 seconds. Righteous Hammer is a Basic Ability which hits all enemies in front of Yrel, dealing damage and Knocking them back. As you channel it, it deals more damage and Knocks enemies farther back. If fully charged up, it also Stuns all enemies hit. As for all Yrel's Basic Abilities, you can activate Divine Purpose right before casting Righteous Hammer to instantly cast it as if you fully charged it up. When doing so, it costs no Mana and cannot be interrupted before going off. Righteous Hammer provides a useful Knockback effect that can be used either offensively or defensively. If used offensively, Yrel can thrust enemy Heroes towards her team and enable an easy takedown. If used defensively, she can push enemy Heroes away and help her team to retreat. The best way to use Righteous Hammer is to fully-charge it (either manually or by using Divine Purpose) for Stunning enemy Heroes. This gives more safety when using it defensively and is more threatening when using it offensively because it blocks enemy Heroes for a moment and allows allied Heroes to follow-up. Righteous Hammer can also be used as an interrupt. When you need to interrupt a stationary channel, all you have to do is cast Righteous Hammer as quickly as possible, without fully-charging it. When you need to interrupt a mobile channel, you have to fully-charge Righteous Hammer (usually by using Divine Purpose).

abilities.title: Avenging Wrath
abilities.text: Leap to a location, dealing 260 (+4% per level) damage to enemies in an area and Slowing them by 60% for 1 second. Charging up this Ability increases its range. Avenging Wrath is a Basic Ability that allows Yrel to leap over a short distance. Upon impact, enemies are damaged and Slowed. As you channel it, its range goes up but its damage stays the same. As for all Yrel's Basic Abilities, you can activate Divine Purpose right before casting Avenging Wrath to instantly cast it as if you fully charged it up. When doing so, it costs no Mana and cannot be interrupted before going off. The best way to use Avenging Wrath is to approach enemy Heroes from the side, charge it while they cannot see you, jump over impassable terrain, activate Divine Purpose, and then cast Righteous Hammer. You can also do something similar by standing in a bush that is uncontested. While laning, you can use this Ability for waveclear, for damaging enemy Heroes, and also for escaping while getting ganked. Do not use Divine Purpose on Avenging Wrath when clearing Minions because it does not deal more damage and you do not instantly need the increased range.

abilities.title: Ardent Defender
abilities.text: Ardent Defender (R) Yrel Heroic Surround Yrel in a barrier for 3 seconds, absorbing all damage taken and healing her for 50% of the damage received. Ardent Defender is a Heroic Ability which makes Yrel take no damage for a few seconds and convert all the damage taken during that time into healing. The more damage she absorbs while active, the more healing she receives. This is such a powerful Heroic Ability that whether it is on cooldown or not dictates how aggressively Yrel can play. When it is on cooldown, you need to play safer. When it is ready to use, you can play more aggressively. In order to guarantee her participation during a team fight once the effect has expired, we recommend using Ardent Defender while Yrel has at least 50% Health remaining. If used while Yrel is on the brink of death, it will usually result in her retreating anyway. The best moment to activate Ardent Defender is when you are going to take a lot of damage. Note that having your Armor reduced (for example, by enemy Structures nearby) increases the healing taken during it. Similarly, having your Armor increased causes you to take less healing from it.

abilities.title: Sacred Ground
abilities.text: Sacred Ground (R) Yrel Heroic Yrel sanctifies the ground around her, gaining 50 Armor until she leaves the area. Sacred Ground is a Heroic Ability which sanctifies a big area at Yrel's feet. Yrel has bonus Armor while standing it and loses it upon leaving. The effect on the ground does not move with Yrel and disappears when she leaves the area. Thanks to its low cooldown, you can use Sacred Ground liberally during the game, simply to take less damage during team fights. When pushing, you can also use it to tank enemy Structures. With a well-time cast, you can mitigate incoming damage from a single powerful Ability (notably Pyroblast by Kael'thas). If you place it near a valuable choke point, it will be easier for you to get value from it because enemy Heroes will not be able to easily avoid that area. When diving, you can also use it to tank enemy Structures, so that you and/or your teammates will be able to play aggressively for longer when there are no Minions, Mercenaries, Monsters, or Summons to tank them for you. Due to its stationary nature, Sacred Ground is countered by Displacement effects that are powerful enough to move Yrel outside of the sanctified area and is best used for having more survivability while controlling valuable choke point during team fights or when contesting a Capture Point for an Objective or Mercenary Camp.

abilities.title: Divine Purpose
abilities.text: Activate to instantly charge Yrel's next Basic Ability at no mana cost. Divine Purpose's cooldown is reduced by 3 seconds if Stunned or Silenced while charging her skills. Passive: Yrel's Basic Abilities charge up over 1.5 seconds, increasing in effectiveness, but reducing Yrel's Movement Speed by 25%. Divine Purpose is a Trait which can be activated to make your next Basic Ability instant cast and cost no Mana. Furthermore, whenever your Basic Abilities are interrupted while being channeled, Divine Purpose's cooldown is reduced by a few seconds. Depending on which situation Yrel finds herself in, she may have to consider triggering a different Basic Ability. Using Divine Purpose to empower Vindication provides a considerable amount of healing and waveclear. Combining it with Righteous Hammer can get her out of dangerous situations or help her allies get kills. Last but not least, Avenging Wrath can be immediately used to either engage a fight swiftly or get Yrel to safety.

Zagara.name: Zagara
Zagara.overview: Zagara is a Ranged Assassin who relies on Zerg summons to wreak havoc on her opponents. Creep Tumor is a strong ability, providing not only buffs to several of her attributes, including attack range and movement speed, but also supplying precious vision throughout the Battleground. Zagara is capable of tearing down enemy defenses from afar and, when left alone for even a small duration, will turn the strongest enemy fortifications into nothing more than heaps of rubble.
strengths: Creep Tumor provides a massive amount of vision throughout the entire battlefield
Able to solo Mercenary Camps with ease
weaknesses: Her only form of hard crowd control is Devouring Maw

build_notes.name: Infested Drop Build
build_notes.text: Zagara's Infested Drop Build allows you to deal a solid amount of damage in team fights, especially in the late game against Heroes who have high maximum Health. In particular, Corpse Feeders at Level 1 and Bile Drop at Level 7 boost the already good damage output of Corrosive Saliva at Level 16.

build_notes.name: Infest Build
build_notes.text: Zagara's Infest Build makes you more powerful when split-pushing but weaker while fighting against enemy Heroes. Due to being vulnerable to ganks as usual, you should not choose this Build when the enemy team has Heroes good for that (for example Zeratul). Infest at Level 1 empowers nearby Minions, so that you can take down enemy Structures with ease, unless the enemy team can quickly clear your Minions. Mutalisk at Level 16 is good for taking down to enemy Structures as well as for dealing with Mercenaries.

build_notes.name: ARAM Build
build_notes.text: Zagara's ARAM Build allows you to deal a solid amount of damage in team fights, especially in the late game against Heroes who have high maximum Health. In particular, Corpse Feeders at Level 1 and Bile Drop at Level 7 boost the already good damage output of Corrosive Saliva at Level 16. See our Talents page for further information » Create your own build and share it with friends!

Zagara.synergy_text: Due to her lack of mobility, Zagara is best when paired with one or two Tanks who can provide her a strong frontline. Those with reliable crowd-control can also set up devastating combos with Zagara's Devouring Maw.
Zagara.counter_text: Zagara is counterd in lane by high mobility Assassins like Illidan, who can outsustain her and stick to her even while on Creep. Furthermore, global range Heroes like Falstad or Dehaka can drastically limit her efficiency while split-pushing.
Zagara.maps_text: Zagara's stronger maps Zagara's average maps Zagara's weaker maps Zagara is particularly good on larger Maps with multiple Objective locations (such as Sky Temple), when she can take advantage of distracted enemy Heroes to split-push uncontested, sometimes even with the help of Nydus Network. Maps that are smaller (such as Tomb of the Spider Queen) make it much more difficult for Zagara to split-push. In those situations, Zagara can still be a great lane bully in the early game and a powerful damage dealer in the late game, thanks to Talents.
Zagara.tips: Baneling Barrage should be used primarily for waveclear to conserve valuable mana. When using Baneling Barrage on Minion Waves, try using it from a 90 degree angle. Aim at the Wizard Minion to maximize splash damage. Use Hunter Killer to zone enemies from team fights or lane. Always use Infested Drop when it is available to deal damage safely and provide vision. Infested Drop can also be used to tank Mercenary Camps and interrupt channeling of objectives (like Tributes on Cursed Hollow). Do not try to force Devouring Maw and instead wait for enemies to come into range. Place Nydus Worms provided by Nydus Network in spots clear of heavy foot-traffic to prevent them from being immediately destroyed. Always use all available Creep Tumors. Place them inside bushes and at other out-of-the-way locations to prevent the enemy from accidentally destroying them with AoE abilities. See our Abilities page for further information »
Zagara.meta_text: Zagara is currently played as Offlaner to dominate the early game against most enemy Heroes unless ganked. When fighting on a widespread area of Creep Tumor, Zagara is a powerful duelist and bully thanks to the Attack Range and Movement Speed provided combined with the relentless single-target damage of Hunter Killer. She is easily able to kite enemies in pursuit of her as well as chase those down who may have regretfully overstepped their boundary. The vision that Creep Tumor provides is extremely powerful to play around enemy ganks, the best way to counter her when she goes in the enemy part of the battlefield to get value from her pushing power.

abilities.title: Baneling Barrage
abilities.text: Recharge Time: 4 seconds Launch 2 Banelings that deal 80 (+4% per level) damage to enemies they hit. Stores up to 2 charges. Baneling Barrage causes Zagara to launch two Banelings in the targeted direction. If a Baneling comes in contact with an enemy or reaches its full range, it explodes and deals splash damage. Up to 2 charges of Baneling Barrage can be stored at one time, so you can shoot a total of 4 Banelings in quick succession. Each charge has a 3-second recharge time. Baneling Barrage is Zagara's primary source of waveclear when in lane. Banelings do not have their own Health and cannot be destroyed until they either hit an enemy or reach the end of their range. Because of this, Banelings make for reliable poke, especially when contesting Objectives that have to be channeled for a few seconds (such as Tributes on Cursed Hollow). Keep in mind that Zagara's primary source of lane harass should come from her Basic Attacks, especially when under the effects of creep. Most opponents will quickly learn to avoid the relatively slow moving Banelings if they are relentlessly cast towards them.

abilities.title: Hunter Killer
abilities.text: Summon a Hydralisk to attack a single target, dealing 71 (+5% per level) damage per second. The Hydralisk loses Health over 10 seconds, and has 500 (+4.5% per level) Health. Hunter Killer summons a Hydralisk to attack a single target. The Hydralisk can be killed and can only attack the target if it has vision. If the target is killed or cannot be found, the Hydralisk will travel to the nearest lane and push for its remaining duration. It despawns after 8 seconds. Hunter Killer is a strong ability that deals a good amount of single-target damage. In lane, Zagara can completely zone out the enemy Hero simply by casting Hunter Killer on them. If they try to fight Zagara or the Hydralisk while it is active, they will take a significant amount of damage from the combination of the Hydralisk and Zagara's Basic Attacks. This allows you to maintain unsurpassed lane control and apply pressure to the surrounding map objectives or structures. In team fights, Hunter Killer will go largely unnoticed, usually allowing it to deal damage for its full duration, although, it may die to significant AoE damage. Hunter Killer should be used on your primary target, and since the Hydralisk will not switch targets once it spawns, it is important to target the correct Hero. Note that the Hydralisk moves at about the same speed as a Hero, so it will struggle to keep up with fleeing Heroes, unless it is moving on Creep.

abilities.title: Infested Drop
abilities.text: Bombard target area with a Zerg Drop Pod for 140 (+4% per level) damage. The pod spawns 2 Roachlings that deal 30 (+4% per level) damage per second and lose Health over 10 seconds. Infested Drop bombards the targeted area with a Zerg Drop Pod, dealing damage. The pod spawns 2 Roaches that behave like minions. They last 8 seconds or until they are killed. Infested Drop has a wide variety of uses. It can be used to deal damage, provide vision, clear minion waves, delay channeling of map objectives (like the tributes on Cursed Hollow), dismount enemy Heroes, or help clear Mercenary Camps. In lane, it can be another valuable method of pushing the minions. Keep in mind that hitting enemy Heroes with the Zerg Drop Pod can be relatively difficult as there is a noticeable delay in cast time. Bile Drop is a quest that not only permanently increases the initial damage of the Zerg Drop Pod, but will also increase its impact radius. When trying to complete this quest, try to focus the drops on enemy Heroes who are affected by crowd control. If you are playing extremely aggressively in lane, you can use Infested Drop behind the enemy Towers. This will provide vision of any Heroes hiding behind the walls, allowing Hunter Killer to be used on them.

abilities.title: Devouring Maw
abilities.text: Devouring Maw (R) Zagara Heroic Summon a Devouring Maw that devours enemies for 4 seconds. Devoured enemies cannot fight and take 94 (+4% per level) damage per second. Usable on Unstoppable enemies. Devouring Maw summons a Devouring Maw at a target location to consume all enemies within its radius. Devoured enemies are unable to take any action and are untargetable for 4 seconds, taking damage each second. Devouring Maw acts as terrain while it exists, preventing Heroes, minions, mercenaries, or creatures from passing through it. Devouring Maw can be a game-changing ability. Hitting multiple enemy Heroes does some damage and can allow your allies, like Jaina and E.T.C., to combo their abilities as soon as they are released from the Maw. However, even if Devouring Maw only hits a single target, it is essentially removing that Hero from play for 4 seconds. If that target is a Healer, it can allow your team to kill Heroes before they can be healed. Devouring Maw also acts as a terrain, allowing you to completely block off choke-points from enemy Heroes that are not devoured by the Maw. The key to using Devouring Maw effectively and getting multi-Hero Maws is to be patient and wait until the right moment. Running into a fight and opening with Devouring Maw almost never works out well, since it is extremely difficult to land in those scenarios. Instead, you want to be engaging the enemy team with your other abilities and Basic Attacks, and use Devouring Maw when the opportunity arises.

abilities.title: Nydus Network
abilities.text: Nydus Network (R) Zagara Heroic Recharge Time: 120 seconds Summon a Nydus Worm on Creep anywhere that Zagara has vision. Zagara can enter a Nydus Worm and travel to any other Nydus Worm by right-clicking near it. While inside a Nydus Worm, Zagara regenerates 10% Health and Mana per second. Stores up to 2 charges. Maximum of 4 Nydus Worms at a time. Passive: Creep spreads 15% farther. Passive: While on Creep, each Basic Attack reduces all of Zagara's cooldowns by 0.4 seconds. Nydus Network summons a Nydus Worm at the target location that you can enter by right-clicking, after channeling for a short duration. You can right-click a location or press "R" to exit at any Nydus Worm around the map. While inside the Nydus Worm, your Health and Mana are restored at an incredibly high rate. Nydus Network can be cast while inside Nydus Network. Zagara exits Nydus Network instantly. You may only summon a Nydus Worm in areas covered by Zagara's creep. Channelling to enter a Nydus Worm can be interrupted by any damage or crowd control effects. You can hold 2 charges of Nydus Network. The fact that Nydus Worms can only be placed on creep is very important to keep in mind. Enemy Heroes may soon begin hunting Nydus Worms once they begin accumulating. They can use their view of your creep on the ground as a clue to the location of Zagara's Worms. For this reason either try to keep the edge of creep harboring a Worm out of sight completely or over-saturate locations containing Worms as to not give opponents any idea as to where to begin looking. When talenting into Endless Creep at level 20, Nydus Network becomes an almost global ability. Zagara should travel from Worm to Worm, placing them deep within hidden locations of enemy territory. Be careful to keep a solid eye on the location of the enemy. Getting caught behind enemy lines at that stage of the match can very quickly end in defeat for Zagara's team.

abilities.title: Creep Tumor
abilities.text: Recharge Time: 18 seconds Lay a Creep Tumor that generates Creep. While on Creep, Zagara moves 20% faster and her summons move 30% faster. Tumors lose Health over 250 seconds and reveal the surrounding area while active. Stores up to 3 charges. Creep Tumor places a Creep Tumor at the targeted location, spawning Creep that gives vision in the surrounding area and gives extra Movement Speed to Zagara and her Summons. Creep only grants vision in areas that are directly within the line-of-sight of its respective Creep Tumor. This means that Creep will not grant vision inside a bush unless the Creep Tumor itself is placed inside the bush or around a corner near impassable terrain. You should prefer placing your Creep Tumors inside bushes whenever possible to maximize your vision. You should also place Creep Tumors at important locations, including common ganking paths, map objectives, and travel routes. For example, you should always place Creep Tumors around the turn-in on Blackheart's Bay or around Boss camps if they are being contested.
