Claim Bell Towers Destroy your enemy's Towers to bring them under your team's control. The more Towers you have, the more damage an Altar will do.

sections.title: Altars
sections.text: The possible configurations of Altars are: top-left and top-right; middle only; bottom only; middle and bottom; top-left, top-right, and middle; top-left, top-right, and bottom. The top 2 Altars always spawn together, with or without another Altar. Altars will spawn based on the following rules: the 1st and 5th Altar spawns must have 3 Altars; the first 6 Altar spawns are randomly selected from the list above, without repetition; the next 4 Altar spawns are randomly selected from the list above, without repetition, excluding the configurations with 3 Altars; the following Altar spawns are randomly selected from the list above, with repetition, excluding the configurations with 3 Altars. This means that, if you keep track of the previous Altar spawns, you will always know the configuration of the 5th, 6th, and 10th Altar spawns way before their locations are displayed on the Minimap.

sections.title: Bell Towers
sections.text:
Bell Towers (Forts and Keeps) are what actually deals damage to the enemy Core when capturing an Altar. So, before capturing an Altar, you should try to control as many Bell Towers as possible. For example, if a Bell Tower is almost destroyed, finish it off and then capture Altars. Bell Towers start as Forts at the beginning of the game and become Keeps when the Waygate opens. This usually happens at 12:00 minutes but it is delayed if there are Altars active. Once they become Keeps, they have more Health and give more Experience. The lights below each Altar represent Bell Towers. The colors work as follow: blue: your team owns the corresponding Bell Tower; yellow: the corresponding Bell Tower is changing ownership; red: the enemy team owns the corresponding Bell Tower.

If a team controls all Bell Towers (also known as 6-cap), the enemy Core is bombarded until the other team gets one of the Bell Towers back. The first shot hits 8 seconds after you destroy the last Bell Tower, the next 6 shots hit once every 6 seconds, and the following shots hit once every 3 seconds. Time Elapsed Total Damage 8 1 14 2 20 3 26 4 32 5 38 6 44 7 47 8 50 9 When destroyed, Bell Towers take 2 seconds to change ownership (to count for the other team's Altar or for a 6-cap bombardment to start) and about 20 seconds to become a Structure again (to deal damage and take damage). A stolen Bell Tower (enemy team's side) will not have an Healing Fountain but a retaken Bell Tower (allied team's side) will have it.

sections.title: Core Ability
sections.text: Cores are Invulnerable and can only take damage from specific mechanics: Altars, Boss Camp, escorting Sappers into the Kill Zone, or 6-capping (getting all Forts and Keeps). Furthermore, Cores can deal heavy damage to enemies who enter the Kill Zone. A few meters in the Kill Zone, right behind the big gates, there is also an invisible barrier that pushes enemy Heroes away whenever they get past it, similarly to when Heroes enter inside the enemy Hall of Storms. The so-called Kill Zone is an extremely dangerous area marked by a visible barrier surrounding each Core on Towers of Doom. Enemies who enter inside that area take 150 damage (+25 per minute, capping at 900 damage after 30:00 minutes) every 0.5 seconds. Furthermore, each hit reduces the Armor of enemy Heroes hit by 20, up to 40. Heroes with Displacement effects (notably Mighty Gust by Falstad) can push enemy Heroes inside it to kill them with ease. Being categorized as Physical Damage, the damage done by the Kill Zone can be reduced by Physical Armor (such as Dauntless by Yrel) or generic Armor (for example, Armor Up by Garrosh), but not by Spell Armor. In addition to that, since it behaves like Basic Attacks, you can fully negate its damage by using Evade (such as Evasion by Illidan) and Parry (like Parry by Varian) effects.

sections.title: Win Conditions
sections.text: To win the game on Towers of Doom, you should count on any of the following win conditions: Map Objective, Split-push.

sections.title: Tips and Tricks
sections.text: Use the first Healing Fountain (2-minute cooldown) before 1:00 minute because the first Objective on this Map activates at 3:00 minutes, so you will have it back in time for that. If you happen to lose a Bell Tower (Fort or Keep) and the enemy team is playing near the Kill Zone of your Core, you can use Displacement effects to move them into it, causing them to take a huge amount of damage. This is usually enough to get a kill as most Heroes cannot survive that. From a tactical standpoint, Core's Health is a resource that can be used to get value elsewhere. You should only be worried to lose Core's Health when you have 10 or less. For this reason, the Boss Camp should only be captured when either team could use it to immediately win the game. Although it is not possible to march towards the enemy Core and end the game there, if your team has a big advantage (at least 3 enemy Heroes are dead), you can still do something equivalent: 6-capping. To do so, quickly split the team in a way that will cause all enemy Bell Towers (Forts and Keeps) to be captured at the same time. See our Map Guides page for further information »

sections.title: Introduction
sections.text: Volskaya Foundry is a 3-lane Map belonging to the Overwatch universe. The signature Objective of this Map is a Capture Point that rewards a Triglav Protector. The team who wins the Objective can pilot the Triglav Protector, a massive Vehicle with 2 seats that can be used to deal damage to enemy Structures and to Shield allied Heroes.

sections.title: Draft Strategy
sections.text: Prefer Strong late game Siege damage for Structures Sustain damage/healing Avoid Effects relying on bushes Effects relying on impassable terrain Weak late game See our Volskaya Foundry Tier List page for further information »

sections.title: Lane Assignments
sections.text: Here you can find one or more formations that are viable on this Map. Keep in mind that positions in lane are not strict and will often change based on the situation.

sections.title: Formation 4-1
sections.text: The go-to formation for Volskaya Foundry is 4-1: 4 Heroes rotate between the middle and the top lane; 1 Hero, the Offlaner, covers the bottom lane.

sections.title: Map Strategy
sections.text: At 0:30 minutes or whenever available, start clearing the allied Fortification Camp and capture it as soon as possible. Do not forget to pick up the Turret! If you are quick enough, you can get a second Turret at the beginning of the first Objective phase. Ideally, you should capture this Mercenary Camp even during the Objective phase. After that, whenever your team has an advantage or you believe that the enemy team is still busy clearing the enemy Fortification Camp, you can capture the neutral Support Camp near the top lane. Do not forget to pick the Biotic Emitter! At 2:15 minutes or 30-40 seconds before the next Objective phase, start clearing the allied Siege Camp and capture it slightly before the Capture Point activates. To make this Mercenary Camp join the lane behind allied Minions, capture it at 2:40 minutes or 10 seconds after a wave of Minions spawned. At 3:00 minutes or whenever the Objective phase starts, make sure to have a durable Hero on the Capture Point. Keep control of it for as much as possible without dying and retreat if needed. Then, whenever your team gets an advantage, try to push out enemy Heroes and win the Objective. In the early game, the Offlaner should keep soaking. If your team wins the Objective, the first Triglav Protector of the game should preferably be used to destroy Structures in the top lane (in preparation for the second Objective phase), the second one should be used to destroy a Fort, and the following ones should be used to destroy a Keep and eventually go Core. In the early game, the Offlaner should keep soaking. If your team loses the Objective, you can either deal damage to the Triglav Protector or dive past it to kill squishy enemy Heroes. In the early game, the Offlaner should keep soaking.

sections.title: Mercenary Camps
sections.text:
As shown in the image below, Volskaya Foundry has a total of 5 Mercenary Camps: 2 Siege Camps (green icon) in the top lane; 1 Support Camp (red icon) between the top and the middle lanes; 2 Fortification Camps (purple icon) between the middle and bottom lanes. Mercenary Camps on Volskaya Foundry disappear from the battlefield once the Triglav Protector has been spawned (unless their Mercenaries are in combat) and reappear only after the Triglav Protector has been killed.

Mercenary Camps indicated with a red icon are immune to Bribe effects.

sections.title: Siege Camp
sections.text: This type of Mercenary Camp features 3 Assault Troopers. Once captured, it spawns the same units fighting for your team in the corresponding lane. When possible, push with them to get more value. Spawn Time Respawn Delay 0:30 minutes 3:00 minutes after its last capture Baseline Experience Experience Scaling 270 Experience +6 Experience per minute (*) (*) For this Mercenary Camp, Experience starts scaling after 1 minute. Assault Troopers are ranged units that can attack enemies from the distance but lack area of effect damage to quickly clear enemy Minions. Once captured, they are capable of damaging enemy Structures without getting in their range.

sections.title: Fortification Camp
sections.text: This type of Mercenary Camp features 1 Mechanic and 1 Turret. Once captured, it leaves a Turret on the ground that can be collected by allied or enemy Heroes. Always kill the Mechanic first because he can repair the Turret while below 80% Health. Spawn Time Respawn Delay 0:30 minutes 2:30 minutes after its last capture Baseline Experience Experience Scaling 460 Experience +10 Experience per minute

sections.title: Turret
sections.text: Turrets are consumable items that, when put on the ground, deal damage to an enemy within range, prioritizing Heroes and dealing double damage to Minions. Since they count as Mercenaries, you can empower them with some Talents (such as Mercenary Queen by Sylvanas) and weaken them with some other Talents (for example Amateur Opponent by Artanis). Turret [F] Item Place a Turret that rapidly attacks nearby enemies for 45 (+2 per minute) damage every 0.5 seconds. Turret lasts for 45 seconds, or until destroyed.

sections.title: Support Camp
sections.text: This type of Mercenary Camp features 1 Support Mech. Once captured, it leaves a Biotic Emitter on the ground that can be collected by allied or enemy Heroes. Spawn Time Respawn Delay 0:30 minutes 3:00 minutes after its last capture Baseline Experience Experience Scaling 625 Experience +10 Experience per minute Due to being Elite, this Mercenary Camp is immune to Bribe effects (such as Covert Mission by Nova).

sections.title: Biotic Emitter
sections.text: Biotic Emitters are consumable items that, when put on the ground, restore Health and Mana of allied Heroes in range. Do not position them too forward, otherwise they will quickly get destroyed by enemy Heroes. Biotic Emitter [F] Item Create a Biotic Emitter that restores 40% of nearby allied Heroes' maximum Health and Mana. Biotic Emitter lasts for 10 seconds, or until destroyed.

sections.title: Map Objective
sections.text:
The signature Objective on Volskaya Foundry is a Capture Point that rewards a Triglav Protector to the team who gets 100% progress first. The winners can pilot the Triglav Protector, a massive Vehicle with 2 seats that can be used to deal damage to enemy Structures and to Shield allied Heroes. Vehicles are Unstoppable. Capture Points will activate 3 seconds after a Hero steps on them, then they will give 2% per second over 45 seconds, pausing when abandoned for more than 12 seconds, and not giving the final reward if contested. Spawn Time Respawn Delay 3:00 minutes 3:00 minutes after the Triglav Protector dies

Capture Points Control points activate occasionally. Stand within them to capture them. Fully capturing a point grants you control of a giant mech. Control the Protector The Triglav Protector mech is controlled by two players: one pilot and one gunner. Work together! Destroy Everything The Protector's abilities deal incredible damage to structures and Heroes alike. Use it to lay waste to your enemy. Once claimed, the Triglav Protector lasts for 50 seconds plus 3 seconds for each minute of Game Time that has passed. Each of the 2 players controlling the Triglav Protector has access to a different set of Abilities (similarly to Cho'Gall) and can decide to exit whenever they want, allowing someone else to enter in their place. The pilot's Basic Attacks deals 100% more damage to enemy Structures. While both seats are occupied, the pilot's Basic Attacks deal 50% more damage and both the pilot's and gunner's Abilities recharge 25% faster and Energy regeneration is increased by 25%. The first player to enter in the Triglav Protector will become the pilot, able to decide where to go, whereas the second one will become the gunner. If only the gunner seat is already taken (because the previous pilot decided to exit) then the next player entering in the Triglav Protector will become the pilot.

sections.title: Triglav Pilot
sections.text: The following Abilities can be used by the player who is in the Triglav Protector's pilot seat. Whoever enters first in a newly spawned Triglav Protector will be the pilot.

sections.title: Charge
sections.text: Charge [Q] Pilot Cooldown: 8 seconds Charge a target and deal 160 (+14 per minute) damage in an area. Non-Heroes take 500% increased damage. Charge should ideally be used to damage enemy Structures because it deals way more damage to non-Heroes or to clear enemy Minions because it can hit many of them, resulting in more damage per cast compared to hitting a single target. Charge should ideally NOT be used on Heroes because it deals way less damage to them.

sections.title: Rocket Fist
sections.text: Rocket Fist [W] Pilot Cooldown: 14 seconds Launch a Rocket Fist that deals 150 (+15 per minute) damage to the first Hero or Structure in its path. The rocket pushes away Heroes for 1.5 seconds and disables Structures for 4 seconds. Minions on its path are instantly killed. Rocket Fist should ideally be used to instantly kill enemy Minions and/or to disable enemy Structures that are attacking someone. Avoid overlapping Shield Emitter to take less damage from enemy Structures and Rocket Fist to disable enemy Structures. In case of emergency, Rocket Fist [W] can be also used to peel for your team, or to interrupt a powerful stationary channeled Ability. (such as Mosh Pit by E.T.C.).

sections.title: Shield Emitter
sections.text: Shield Emitter [E] Pilot Cooldown: 16 seconds Gain 25 Armor for 3 seconds and give nearby allied Heroes a Shield that absorbs 500 (+50 per minute) damage over 3 seconds. Shield Emitter should be used to save allied Heroes from incoming damage and/or to reduce damage taken by the Triglav Protector, especially when in range of enemy Structures that are not disabled by Rocket Fist. Avoid overlapping Shield Emitter to take less damage from enemy Structures and Rocket Fist to disable enemy Structures.

sections.title: Triglav Gunner
sections.text: The following Abilities can be used by the player that is in the Triglav Protector's gunner seat. Whoever enters second in a newly spawned Triglav Protector will be the gunner.

sections.title: Particle Cannon
sections.text: Particle Cannon [Q] Gunner Cooldown: 4 seconds Start extending the range of the Particle Cannon. Reactivate to fire, dealing 190 (+19 per minute) damage in the targe area. Particle Cannon should ideally be used to clear enemy Minions because it can hit many of them, resulting in more damage per cast compared to hitting a single target.

sections.title: Gatling Cannon
sections.text: Gatling Cannon [W] Gunner Toggle to fire missiles at the cursor's location. Each missile deals 38 (+3.8 per minute) damage but drains 1 Energy. Reactivate to stop firing. Deals 50% less damage to Structures. Gatling Cannon should ideally be used to hit enemy Heroes because it deals 50% less damage to enemy Structures. To maximize cooldown usage, you should stop using Gatling Cannon when Particle Cannon and Scorching Laser are ready to use again. To maximize Energy usage, you should be using Gatling Cannon when having maximum Energy or close to maximum Energy.

sections.title: Scorching Laser
sections.text: Scorching Laser [E] Gunner Cooldown: 10 seconds Vector Targeting Draw a line on the ground, dealing 60 (+6 per minute) damage. After 1 second, it explodes for 380 (+38 per minute) damage. Due to its delay, Scorching Laser should generally be used to damage enemy Structures (ideally 2-3 at the same time), however, it can also be used on enemy Heroes who cannot move for about 1 second because of crowd control effects. ! How to use Vehicles Vehicles have two resources: Health and duration. If they time out with high Health, it means you played too safe. If they get destroyed while there is still a lot of duration remaining, it means you played too aggressive. As a general rule, you want to keep the percentage values of Health and duration balanced. When pushing with a won Objective, you should still avoid being caught alone and not fight when outnumbered, especially when going for Keeps. If your Vehicle gets destroyed deep in the enemy territory, you will not be able to reach a safe area before getting killed unless you have a lot of mobility. In the early game, when multiple enemy Forts are still up, Vehicles can also be used as a distraction, not just for pushing directly. While they clear enemy Minions and threaten enemy Structures, the rest of the team can push in another lane. The enemy team will have to split for defending multiple lanes at the same time.

sections.title: Core Ability
sections.text: Every 6 seconds, the Core shoots 3 Rocket Fists at nearby enemy Heroes, dealing 150 damage and Knocking them back.

sections.title: Win Conditions
sections.text: To win the game on Volskaya Foundry, you should count on any of the following win conditions: Map Objective, Split-push. Try to store Turrets and Biotic Emitters for the late game.

sections.title: Tips and Tricks
sections.text: Use the first Healing Fountain (2-minute cooldown) before 1:00 minute because the first Objective on this Map activates at 3:00 minutes, so you will have it back in time for that. Global Heroes should ideally take care of the lane that is farther away from the next Objective location, so that they can use their global tool to quickly join their team during the next Objective phase. We recommend to let a non-Healer pick the Biotic Emitter, so that it can be used to heal the Healer if they happen to be under crowd control or to heal your team when your Healer is dead. The pilot slot of the Triglav Protector should be filled with a squishy Hero because leaving them outside while durable Heroes (usually with crowd control usable to peel) are inside would make your backline vulnerable to dive. The gunner slot of the Triglav Protector can either be filled with another squishy Hero or left empty, so that whoever is in danger can enter in it to protect themselves from enemy damage. Note that taking damage does not interrupt the channel to enter in it. When piloting the Triglav Protector, you should generally use: Charge [Q] to damage enemy Structures or to clear grouped enemy Minions; Rocket Fist [W] to instantly kill enemy Minions and/or to disable enemy Structures; and Shield Emitter [E] to gain Armor while under attack and/or to Shield allied Heroes. In case of emergency, Rocket Fist [W] can be also used to peel for your team, or to interrupt a powerful stationary channeled Ability (such as Mosh Pit by E.T.C.). When being the gunner in the Triglav Protector, you should generally use: Particle Cannon [Q] to clear enemy Minions when they are grouped; Gatling Cannon [W] to damage enemy Heroes when your other Abilities are on cooldown (stop using it when they are usable again); and Scorching Laser [E] to damage enemy Structures and/or crowd controlled enemy Heroes. Heroes with percent damage (such as Drain Hope by Leoric) are the best for defending from enemy Vehicles. In case that is your Offlaner and it is early game, you may want to send someone else to soak in the lane they left. Remember that Cursed Bullet by Greymane and Sleep Dart by Ana cannot hit Vehicles. If your team has a Hero with a powerful Quest that requires hitting enemy Heroes (for example Zul'jin), you could let the enemy team get an early game Triglav Protector to easily get Quest stacks while defending from it. If your team is doing fine, you can store Turrets and Biotic Emitters for the late game instead of using them in the early game. If you are going to die, however, place them on the ground before they kill you and steal them. If the enemy team is not contesting the Objective and you step out of the Capture Point, you get 26% additional progress. This means you can leave the Capture Point at 74% progress and still get a Triglav Protector. Similarly, if you want to wait for allied Heroes before getting a Triglav Protector, you should leave the Capture Point before reaching 74% progress. At high level of play it is common to completely ignore the Objective area and get value elsewhere by pushing because the Triglav Protector takes too much time to be unlocked and can generally be defended without much difficulty, sometimes after diving and killing whoever is outside of it. See our Map Guides page for further information »

sections.title: Introduction
sections.text: Warhead Junction is a 3-lane Map belonging to the Starcraft universe. The signature Objective of this Map are Warheads. They can be collected and launched on a target location, usually to damage enemy Structures. On this Map, you can also find the Slime Boss, a unique Mercenary Camp that deals a huge amount of damage to enemy Heroes and Structures.

sections.title: Draft Strategy
sections.text: Prefer Anchor Gankers Global presence Point control for Boss Camp Poke tools for Objective Self-sustain Split-push Avoid Quests to stack on Heroes See our Warhead Junction Tier List page for further information »

sections.title: Lane Assignments
sections.text: Here you can find one or more formations that are viable on this Map. Keep in mind that positions in lane are not strict and will often change based on the situation.

sections.title: Formation 3-1-1
sections.text:
The go-to formation for Warhead Junction is 3-1-1:

3 Heroes cover the top lane and push as much as possible; 1 Hero, the Offlaner, covers the middle lane; 1 Hero, the Anchor, covers the bottom lane.

sections.title: Map Strategy
sections.text: At 0:30 minutes or whenever available, start clearing the allied Bruiser Camp and capture it as soon as possible. To make this Mercenary Camp join the lane behind allied Minions, capture it at 0:45 minutes or 15 seconds after a wave of Minions spawned. At 2:30 minutes or 30-40 seconds before the next Objective phase, start clearing the allied Siege Camp in the bottom lane and capture it slightly before the Warheads spawn. To make this Mercenary Camp join the lane in front of allied Minions, capture it at 2:35 minutes or 5 seconds after a wave of Minions spawned. During the Objective phase, get at least half the Warheads and use them to open the battlefield at your advantage. If possible, poke enemy Heroes who are trying to collect a Warhead and interrupt enemy Heroes who are trying to launch them on your Structures. After about 10:00 minutes, whenever your team has an advantage, regardless if there is an Objective to contest or not, you can capture the Boss Camp and push with it. Avoid doing it earlier if you do not have a dedicated team composition.

sections.title: Mercenary Camps
sections.text:
As shown in the image below, Warhead Junction has a total of 5 Mercenary Camps: 1 Boss Camp (red icon) in the top lane; 2 Bruiser Camps (blue icon) in the top lane; 2 Siege Camps (green icon) in the bottom lane. Mercenary Camps on Warhead Junction are always active, even when Warheads are available on the battlefield.

Mercenary Camps indicated with a red icon are immune to Bribe effects.

sections.title: Siege Camp
sections.text: This type of Mercenary Camp features 2 Hellbats. Once captured, it spawns the same units fighting for your team in the corresponding lane. When possible, push with them to get more value. Spawn Time Respawn Delay 0:30 minutes 3:00 minutes after its last capture Baseline Experience Experience Scaling 120 Experience +4 Experience per minute (*) (*) For this Mercenary Camp, Experience starts scaling 1 minute later. Hellbats reduce the Armor of enemy Structures and Heroes hit by their cleaving Basic Attacks for 3 seconds by 4 Armor per Basic Attack, stacking 5 times, for a maximum of 20 Armor reduction.

sections.title: Bruiser Camp
sections.text: This type of Mercenary Camp features 3 Goliaths and 1 Raven. Once captured, it spawns the same units fighting for your team in the corresponding lane. When possible, push with them to get more value. Spawn Time Respawn Delay 0:30 minutes 4:00 minutes after its last capture Baseline Experience Experience Scaling 270 Experience +8 Experience per minute (*) (*) For this Mercenary Camp, Experience starts scaling 1 minute later. Ravens do not use Basic Attacks. Instead, they fire a Seeker Missile (5-second cooldown) which Reveals the targeted Hero and damages them upon impact. Ravens deal only 20 (not scaling) damage per second whereas Goliaths deal 40 (+1 per minute) damage per second.

sections.title: Boss Camp
sections.text: This type of Mercenary Camp features 1 Slime Boss. Once captured, it spawns the same unit fighting for your team in the corresponding lane. When possible, push with it to get more value. Spawn Time Respawn Delay 5:00 minutes 5:00 minutes after its last capture Baseline Experience Experience Scaling 750 Experience +10 Experience per minute (*) (*) For this Mercenary Camp, Experience starts scaling 1 minute later. While in combat, the Slime Boss will use Slime Spit (14-second cooldown) to create a damaging pool on the ground, so be ready to avoid it. About 6 seconds after that, the boss will cast Spawn Pods (14-second cooldown) to launch multiple slime pods around him. Due to being Elite, this Mercenary Camp is immune to Bribe effects (such as Covert Mission by Nova).

sections.title: Map Objective
sections.text:
The signature Objective of Warhead Junction are Warheads (also called Nukes). To pick them up, Heroes have to channel for 5 seconds. Warheads also spawn a Regeneration Globe when collected from their spawn location. Collecting a Warhead will allow Heroes to nuke a given area and damage all enemy units within it. Due to their relatively long cast time and huge delay, Warheads are best used for damaging enemy Structures. Spawn Time Respawn Delay 3:00 minutes 2:55 minutes after collecting all Warheads

Warhead Deployment Multiple Warheads will spawn periodically across the battleground. Collect Warheads Pick up a Warhead to activate your Nuke. Use it or you will drop it when you die! Call Down the Thunder Launch Nukes to burn enemy team's fortifications. Attack their structures to extend the burn!

sections.title: Warheads
sections.text: Warheads can spawn in 9 possible locations over 3 rows (top, middle, and bottom). Warhead will be distributed evenly in each lane: if there is only 1 Warhead, it will be at the center; if there are 2 Warheads, they will be on the sides. Every spawn will feature from 2 to 4 Warheads. Spawns with 2 Warheads will have them on separate lanes. Spawns with 3 Warheads or more will always have exactly one lane with 2 Warheads. The number of Warheads depends on the Objective phase's number: the 1st Objective phase can have from 2 to 3 Warheads; the 4th Objective phase can have from 3 to 4 Warheads; any other Objective phase can only have exactly 2 Warheads. The 1st spawn has two additional rules: when there are 2 Warheads, they will be both middle; when there are 3 Warheads, they will be 1 middle, 2 in a side lane, and 0 in the other. The 4th spawn has an additional rule: when there are 3 Warheads, they will be 2 in a lane and 1 in another; when there are 4 Warheads, they will be 1 top, 2 middle, and 1 bottom. After collecting a Warhead, it will be on cooldown for 5 seconds. If you do not pay attention to this characteristic, you may end up walking within range of enemy Structures by mistake, taking unnecessary damage or even dying in the process. Also, Warheads deal damage after 4 seconds, so you will rarely hit enemy Heroes. Warhead [F] Item After a 3 second channel and a 4 second delay, launch a Warhead dealing 1750 (+70 per minute for 25 minutes) damage. Structures are also ignited for 10 seconds, taking 120 (+4.8 per minute for 25 minutes) damage per second. Heroic Basic Attacks pause the burning's duration for 3 seconds. Forts, Keeps, and Core take 125% more damage. Try to hit multiple Structures at the same time to maximize their value. Using 1 Warhead on each Fort (while also hitting nearby Towers) is more efficient than using 3 Warheads on the same Fort (while also hitting nearby Towers). That said, considering that Forts, Keeps, and Core take 125% more damage from Warheads, you should not hesitate to use a Warhead for damaging a Fort without Towers nearby or a Keep without Towers nearby. Due to their cast time and delay, you will rarely hit enemy Heroes with them. The only situation in which it makes sense to use a Warhead not to hit enemy Structures is when trying to secure a Boss Camp because it will help you kill the Boss faster and, more importantly, will zone enemy Heroes because they will not want to take a lot of damage from its impact. You can use the Warhead timings provided below to launch a Warhead when the Game Time shows the corresponding amount of seconds. This way you can instantly kill a wave of enemy Minions for free when using a Warhead to hit a Fort or Keep and its nearby Towers at the same time. When targeting a Fort and its nearby Towers, the Warhead timings are: Top: 16 seconds, 46 seconds; Middle: 9 seconds, 39 seconds; Bottom: 17 seconds, 57 seconds. When targeting a Keep and its nearby Towers, the Warhead timings are: Top: 29 seconds, 59 seconds; Middle: 28 seconds; 58 seconds; Bottom: 29 seconds, 59 seconds. Heroes trying to use a Warhead can be interrupted with crowd-control Abilities, putting the Warhead on a 5-second cooldown. To defend from Warheads, stay near your Structures to constantly stop enemy Heroes for nuking them. At the same time, though, enemy Heroes will try to use Warheads from the sides, behind the impassable terrain surrounding your Forts. Do not bother trying to reduce the damage done by enemy Heroes who are launching a Warhead. Their damage cannot be affected by damage reduction effects (such as Defense Matrix by D.Va). Once a Warhead goes off, the only way to protect your Structures from its damage is putting them in Time Stop (only possible with Void Prison by Zeratul) right before the damage happens. Whenever a Hero having a Warhead dies, that Warhead will drop on the ground, ready to be collected by another allied or enemy Hero. If you predict that you are going to die for sure in the next 3 seconds, you can use it on the spot so that the enemy team will not be able to get value from it. Note that this move is impossible to pull off against enemy Heroes who can quickly burst you down or have interrupts. Warheads stop scaling when picked up. For example, a Warhead picked up at 3:05 minutes will do about 700 less damage than a Warhead picked up at 13:05 minutes. This difference may occasionally be relevant when trying to take down a Keep in the late game or when going for the enemy Core. Store some Warheads for when you will try to end the game because they can deal a lot of damage to the enemy Core. When using Warheads to end the game, aim the Warheads more towards your team, so that they will not only hit the enemy Core but also zone enemy Heroes away from you. Assuming the enemy Core has 20-minute scaling (maximum possible) and Warheads have about 17-minute scaling (realistic scenario), each Warhead will deal damage on impact equal to about 30% of the enemy Core's maximum Health (stacking) and damage over time equal to about 20% of the enemy Core's maximum Health (not stacking). Warheads Impact Damage Damage Over Time Total Damage 1 30% 20% 50% 2 60% 20% 80% 3 90% 20% 110% 4 120% 20% 140% 5 150% 20% 170% Note that Cores have a Shield equal to 50% of their maximum Health. As a consequence, if you want to destroy the enemy Core to win the game, you need to deal damage equal to 150% of the enemy Core's maximum Health.

sections.title: Sewage Tunnel
sections.text:
Even if Warhead Junction is a big Map, it is relatively fast to travel between the bottom and the top lane thanks to the Sewage Tunnel connecting them. When clicking on it, after channeling for 2 seconds, you will be teleported to the other side of the tunnel. You cannot use the Sewage Tunnel while directly taking damage from enemies.

You can use the Sewage Tunnel for various things, such as: when you are in the top lane but the enemy team is trying to siege your Structures in the bottom lane; to surprise enemy Heroes with a gank; as a valuable shortcut when traveling from a Mercenary Camp to the furthest lane, or in the opposite direction. All that said, avoid using them if your team is not controlling at least one of the Watch Towers because, thanks to them, the enemy team will see all your movements between the bottom and top lane on the Minimap, indirectly gaining a tactical advantage by knowing your approximate position in the next few seconds and because, due to not having them, you will risk meeting enemy Heroes at the exit of the Sewage Tunnel.

sections.title: Watch Towers
sections.text:
Warhead Junction features 2 Watch Towers: one right above the middle lane and another slightly below it, each of them giving vision on one of the entrances of the Sewage Tunnel.

Securing a Watch Tower provides your team with greater vision, allowing you to keep an eye on enemy movements in that part of the battlefield. Watch Towers can be captured by standing in the area until your team gains control. After 45 seconds of not being occupied, they become neutral again. Because of this, they should only be captured when you are playing in that area for other reasons (either to capture Mercenary Camps or for contesting the Objective). Watch Towers controlled by the enemy team are extremely dangerous, especially when there are bushes nearby, therefore you should think twice before contesting them. If you do not have mobility tools at your disposal and your teammates are not nearby to help you, you should definitely not try to capture a Watch Tower as you will only risk dying for no reason. Staying alive is more important than getting vision.

sections.title: Core Ability
sections.text: Every 18 seconds, the Core launches a Warhead at a nearby enemy Hero, dealing 30% maximum Health as damage to enemy Heroes hit.

sections.title: Win Conditions
sections.text: To win the game on Warhead Junction, you should count on any of the following win conditions: Boss Camp, Split-push, storing Warheads for hitting Core.

sections.title: Tips and Tricks
sections.text: Use the first Healing Fountain (2-minute cooldown) before 1:00 minute because the first Objective on this Map activates at 3:00 minutes, so you will have it back in time for that. Warheads do NOT deal bonus damage in the center area. In order to maximize their damage, Warheads should ideally be used to hit as many Structures as possible at the same time. Note that Forts, Keeps, and Core take 125% more damage from them. Warheads make enemy Structures hit take damage over time. Heroic Basic Attacks can make the damage over time last longer. To get value from this, use Warheads when accompanied by allied Heroes to help you and allied Minion to tank enemy Structures for you. Watch Towers controlled by the enemy team are extremely dangerous, especially when there are bushes nearby, therefore you should think twice before contesting them. Before using the Sewage Tunnel for rotating between top lane and bottom lane, it is important to look at the Minimap and be aware of where enemy Heroes could be. See our Map Guides page for further information »

guides.title: Opening moves
guides.blurb: What to do in the first minute: group, siege, gank, trap or split.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.text: There are various strategies that can be used in the first minute of a game, each one with a different set of advantages and disadvantages. In this guide we take a look at each opening move in order to understand when and why they are played, as well as how to counter them.

sections.title: Group Opening
sections.text: The group opening consists of having your whole team in the same lane for around 30 seconds, soak all Experience from the first wave of Minions, and then immediately split across all lanes to start soaking Experience there as well. As you may know already, the group opening is the most common one on 3-lane Maps. The viability of this strategy is based on the fact that Minions take slightly more time to clash with enemy Minions on side lanes compared to the middle lane, something that is not true for 2-lane Maps. Your team should not automatically go for the group opening because, compared to the enemy team, a given team will often have more tools to be able to get more value from that kind of start. The loading screen is a good moment to evaluate which team can get more value from an early brawl and to choose your opening move accordingly. Being all together makes it easier to clear the first wave of Minions without risking to be engaged when outnumbered, something that can easily happen if the enemy team chooses the group opening but your team goes for the split opening instead. To make it simpler for everyone, wait for Minions to stop walking and then start clearing them. By not allocating too many Heroes in a side lane, you do not risk that the enemy team surprises you with a siege opening in the middle lane or, even worse, in the opposite side lane. If you are not ready to quickly rotate there, an enemy team with a lot of siege power will be able to take down at least a Tower for free, so you better have most if not all Heroes in the middle lane until you see where the enemy Heroes are. While playing on Maps where the 4-man prefers to rotate between 2 lanes, the team who perform better during the first brawl (either by having more waveclear or by having more kill potential) will have a rotation advantage, meaning that they will tend to clear the next few waves of Minions slightly before the enemy team. When a team is leading the rotation, it becomes easier for them to harass enemy Heroes who are trying to rotate and further slow down their clearing speed by zoning or even dismounting them. Considering that it can easily result in a team fight, the group opening is great for Heroes featuring Quests that must be stacked by interacting with enemy Heroes and is bad for Heroes who have a weak early game but a strong late game or, more in general, that are too weak in team fights at the beginning of the game. While going from a lane to another, be careful that the enemy team isn't going for a trap opening! If they aren't in vision and you cannot see them on the Minimap, you better take a safer but longer route because dying will cause you to lose a lot of Experience from Minions, in addition to the Experience the enemy team will gain from killing you.

sections.title: Siege Opening
sections.text: The siege opening is executed by playing in the opposite way compared to the group opening as it consists of having your whole team in a side lane. Be aware that this tactic only works when your team has enough siege power to quickly take down a Tower and the enemy team is slow to rotate there. All we are trying to do while playing is to slowly build an advantage for the late game by taking favorable trades during the course of the game, therefore any damage done to enemy Structures is welcome, even if we do not end up destroying them immediately. If while the game is loading you notice that the enemy team has a lot of siege power, stay on your Mount and grouped approximately in the middle of the battlefield (even on 2-lane Maps), so that you will be able to immediately rotate where the enemy team appears to defend, regardless of which lane they will choose. A team featuring The Lost Vikings on big Maps (for example Cursed Hollow) can easily execute this strategy because they will not need to think about soaking Experience from lanes anymore; instead, they will be sieging as a group of 4 Heroes while the enemy team will struggle to defend as it will not be easy for them to keep 4 Heroes in that lane and at the same time cover two lanes with a single Hero, unless they can double soak and the Map is not that big. There is a team composition featuring Lt. Morales with Medivac Dropship, Tyrael with Sanctification, and 3 Heroes who can deal a lot of siege damage which heavily prefers to start this way, to the point that on some Maps (for example Infernal Shrines) they will immediately focus the Fort in a side lane from the side instead of taking down the Towers first because they do not care about dying in the process, especially in the early game where killing Heroes is worth less than clearing a wave of Minions. In short, the whole Medivac Backdoor strategy (also called Juice Pirates) consists of taking down a Fort before Level 10, use Medivac Dropship to go straight for a Keep at Level 10 with the help of Sanctification to protect the whole team in the process, and then use Medivac Dropship again to go for the enemy Core for doing the same thing.

sections.title: Gank Opening
sections.text: The gank opening consists of trying to kill an isolated enemy Hero (usually the enemy Offlaner) by committing at least 2 Heroes (usually your Tank and your Offlaner) in a side lane in case of 3-lane Maps or in the top lane for 2-lane Maps. To execute this strategy, your ganking squad needs tools to easily punish enemy Heroes that are alone in lane: crowd control to stop their retreat or mobility to chase them, and enough damage to take them down before they get to safety. Once you kill the enemy Hero that was taking care of that lane, you can deal siege damage to enemy Towers before someone comes or, alternatively, you can try to stop whoever is coming there to soak Experience. To play against this strategy, do not clear the wave of Minions in your lane, else you will have to expose for soaking Experience; instead, try to freeze it near your Towers, so that enemy Heroes cannot surprise you from the side or from behind and you can quickly retreat to safety when necessary. A team featuring The Lost Vikings on medium-sized Maps (for example Infernal Shrines) can easily use this strategy because they will not need to think about soaking Experience from lanes anymore; instead, they will be roaming in a group of 4 Heroes from a lane to another and attempting to catch enemy Heroes off-guard with constant ganks. If you are playing a Hero who can easily escape (such as Muradin), you can try to slow down enemy Heroes who are trying to rotate there so that they will not be able to reach that side lane in time to soak all the Experience from its Minions, causing an Experience difference in your team's favor.

sections.title: Trap Opening
sections.text: The trap opening consists of hiding in a bush and waiting for the enemy team to expose. The best locations to use this tactic are the paths where, on 3-lane Maps, enemy Heroes will walk from the middle lane to side lanes because most teams tend to group middle by going for the group opening and someone will eventually need to rotate to a side lane, hopefully by walking right into your trap without checking the bush you are hiding in. As soon as an enemy Hero gets nearby the bush you are hiding in, engage them before they get an opportunity to either check the bush or simply walk away. If you manage to get a kill, try to stop the rest of their team to cover a side lane, something that should be easy while they lack a Hero, however, do not forget to soak Experience from enemy Minions as well. To play around this strategy, if you notice that some or all enemy Heroes are missing from the Minimap, either take a long but safe path while rotating to a side lane or check bushes on your way there. You can check them by using long-range Abilities that give vision or just skillshot-based Abilities as they give vision for a brief moment.

sections.title: Split Opening
sections.text: The split opening consists of skipping the middle brawl by immediately distributing Heroes across all lanes (usually 1-3-1 on 3-lane Maps and 1-4 on 2-lane Maps), resulting in a relatively safe start for your team as no one will need to rotate between lanes to soak Experience from enemy Minions and risk to be ganked or trapped right at the start of the game. You can go for this strategy when your team features Heroes who are not that good in team fight, especially if they have high waveclear to shove enemy Minions before enemy Heroes can come to soak Experience. Avoid this strategy when your team features a lot of Heroes that needs to interact with enemy Heroes to stack their Quests or when the enemy team has a lot of siege power that you want to counter by staying grouped in the same lane where they are, both cases where the group opening will perform better than the split one. When your team is going for the split opening, be extremely careful in lane because the enemy team could be playing for a gank opening instead. To play around that, if you do not see some enemy Heroes on the Minimap for a few seconds, assume they are coming for you or that they are already in the closest bush on your side. See our Map Guides for further information »

guides.title: Pings guide
guides.blurb: What each ping means and how to use them to talk without chat.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.text: Pings are a way to communicate with teammates without using chat. They can be used to coordinate team actions and warn about threats. By effectively communicating through pings, you can keep typing to a minimum and increase your chance to win.

sections.title: Quick Ping
sections.text: To use a Quick Ping with the default Hotkeys, you have to press [Alt + Left Mouse Button] on interactive targets. To customize it, look for Quick Ping in the Advanced tab of the Hotkeys window.

sections.title: Capture Camp
sections.text: Malfurion wants to capture Siege Camp You can use a Quick Ping on a Mercenary Camp to point out that it is time to start clearing it, so that your teammates do not forget to do it. Ping earlier if you do not want them to be late. This way you will also help players who are not familiar with Mercenary Camp timings at understanding when to do them.

sections.title: Get Objective
sections.text: E.T.C. wants to collect Tribute You can use a Quick Ping on a Map Objective to ask your teammates to collect/capture it because you are ready to zone for them or you are busy doing something else. Heroes that are good at zoning should ideally not be channeling Objectives.

sections.title: Push Structure
sections.text: Sylvanas wants to push Tower You can use a Quick Ping on a Structure to tell your teammates to target it or that you ideally want to destroy it before retreating. This is particularly useful when going for a Tower and both Towers near a Gate are up, or when an allied Hero gets thrown behind the enemy Gate and you need quickly to destroy a side Wall to get them out.

sections.title: Kill Hero
sections.text: Anub'arak wants to kill Whitemane You can use a Quick Ping on an enemy Hero in-vision to tell your teammates to kill them. This is a way to communicate that it is important to kill that Hero first or that you want to focus damage on that Hero to secure a kill, avoiding damaging multiple Heroes and killing none.

sections.title: Kill Mercenary
sections.text: Uther wants to kill Boss You can use a Quick Ping on an enemy Mercenary in lane to tell your teammates to kill them. This is a way to communicate that it is important to kill that Mercenary as soon as possible, before nearby Structures take too much damage or get completely destroyed. This is mostly useful for Bosses, but can also be used for other Mercenaries.

sections.title: Need Help
sections.text: Ana needs help! You can use a Quick Ping on yourself to tell your teammates to help you. This is particularly useful when you are being dove while playing a Hero with no (or almost none) peeling tools and low survivability (for example Ana).

sections.title: Healing Fountain
sections.text: Diablo needs to drink from Healing Fountain You can use a Quick Ping on a Healing Fountain to tell your teammates that you need to drink from it. This way they will know that you cannot help them for a few moments. This is better than pinging your Health Bar or Resource Bar (as explained in the corresponding sections) because sometimes you may want to pre-tap (using your Healing Fountain right before a fight when almost full Health and Mana).

sections.title: Danger Ping
sections.text: To use a Danger Ping with the default Hotkeys, you have to press [Alt + Left Mouse Button], move your mouse cursor upwards, and then release. To customize it, look for Quick Ping in the Advanced tab of the Hotkeys window.

sections.title: Dangerous Area
sections.text: Tyrande warns this area is dangerous! You can use a Danger Ping to tell your teammates that a given area is dangerous because there are enemy Heroes hiding nearby or because an enemy Hero put something harmful there (for example Steel Trap by Junkrat).

sections.title: Stealth Hero
sections.text: Garrosh warns this area is dangerous! You can use a Danger Ping to signal that you spotted an enemy Hero in Stealth near that location. Considering that Stealth prevents Heroes to be seen on the Minimap, it is quite useful to use pings for them.

sections.title: Dangerous Hero
sections.text: Varian warns that Garrosh is dangerous! You can use a Danger Ping on an enemy Hero to let your teammates know they are a threat and they should be respecting them. This is useful when facing Heroes with powerful Abilities who can easily get a kill (for example Stitches with Gorge).

sections.title: Bad Positioning
sections.text: Uther warns Jaina is in danger! You can use a Danger Ping on an allied Hero to let them know they are standing in a dangerous spot, a choke point, or where your team lacks vision. This way they will hopefully notice their mistake and move to a safer position before it is too late.

sections.title: Enemy Nearby
sections.text: Varian warns this area is dangerous! You can use a Danger Ping where you think enemy Heroes could engage, flank, invade a Mercenary Camp, or gank. This is meant to raise awareness, to make your teammates faster at responding to threats.

sections.title: Invade Risk
sections.text: Valla warns this area is dangerous! You can use a Danger Ping on a Mercenary Camp to communicate that you believe the enemy team is on it and your team needs to make a play based on that: take down Structures nearby or, if they are on a Boss Camp on a Map with 2 of them, capture the other one.

sections.title: Cheese Risk
sections.text: Mal'Ganis warns that Sgt. Hammer is dangerous! Mal'Ganis warns this area is dangerous! Mal'Ganis warns this area is dangerous! You can use a Quick Ping on an enemy Hero (for example Sylvanas) followed by a Danger Ping on top lane and bottom lane at the start of the game to let your team know that the enemy team could go there immediately and push. If you are near them, defend. If you are too far from that lane, just push and trade Fort for Fort.

sections.title: Hearthstone
sections.text: Sgt. Hammer warns this area is dangerous! Right after returning to the Hall of Storms with your Hearthstone, you can use a Danger Ping on yourself or around you to communicate that you are far away from the action and they need to wait for you.

sections.title: On My Way Ping
sections.text: To use an On My Way Ping with the default Hotkeys, you have to press [Alt + Left Mouse Button], move your mouse cursor to the right, and then release. To customize it, look for Quick Ping in the Advanced tab of the Hotkeys window.

sections.title: Join Soon
sections.text: Anduin is on the way! You can use an On My Way Ping to communicate that you will soon be in a given location to fight, gank, defend Structures, contest Objective, heal allied Heroes, or provide support in any way. This way your teammates could wait for you before making a play or start baiting enemies right before you get there.

sections.title: Capture Camp
sections.text: Greymane is on their way to Bruiser Camp! You can use an On My Way Ping to communicate that you are leaving your current location to go capture a Mercenary Camp. This way your team will be warned that you are abandoning them for a bit and they will realize they have to play safe until you come back.

sections.title: Engage Soon
sections.text: Hanzo is on the way! You can use an On My Way Ping right before engaging (for example Hanzo using Dragon's Arrow), so that your teammates can go in at the same time and not be late. You can also do this during a team fight to communicate that you intend to continue the battle, that you want to chase enemy Heroes.

sections.title: Assist Ping
sections.text: To use an Assist Ping with the default Hotkeys, you have to press [Alt + Left Mouse Button], move your mouse cursor downwards, and then release. To customize it, look for Quick Ping in the Advanced tab of the Hotkeys window.

sections.title: Mercenary Camp
sections.text: Hanzo asks for assistance! You can use an Assist Ping when you or someone else needs help for capturing a Mercenary Camp as the only Hero who is currently on that job is not enough. When this ping is used this way, you generally want the Healer to join.

sections.title: Get Objective
sections.text: Cassia wants assistance capturing this Seed! You can use an Assist Ping when you need help to capture/collect an Objective. This way you can tell your team that you cannot do it alone because there are Heroes and/or Monsters nearby.

sections.title: Cover Lane
sections.text: Tyrande asks for assistance! You can use an Assist Ping when a lane is empty and someone should be there to soak. This way your teammates will notice that someone should go there in order for your team to not lose precious Experience, especially in the early game.

sections.title: Reinforcements
sections.text: Murky asks for assistance! You can use an Assist Ping when a lane is not empty but you need reinforcements due to an unfavorable matchup, due to being outnumbered, or because you cannot win the nearby Capture Point. The help you need could be in various forms: healing, waveclear, or ganking.

sections.title: Regeneration Globe
sections.text: Kael'thas asks for assistance! You can use an Assist Ping on enemy Minions to signal that you need help to collect the Regeneration Globe. While some Heroes need them more than others, they are useful for all Heroes, not just for who has a Quest requiring them. This way a Hero with more mobility or survivability than you can pick it up for you. Regeneration Globes are needed for getting progress on the following Quests: Circle of Life at Level 1 on Alexstrasza; Regeneration Master at Level 1 on Anub'arak; New Habits at Level 1 on Blaze; Freshest Ingredients at Level 1 on Chen; Tissue Regeneration at Level 1 on Dehaka; Prog Rock at Level 1 on E.T.C.; Chaotic Energy at Level 1 on Gul'dan; Fingers of Frost at Level 1 on Jaina; Laws of Hope at Level 1 on Johanna; Mana Addict at Level 1 on Kael'thas; Phylactery of Kel'Thuzad at Level 4 on Kel'Thuzad; Catching Fire at Level 4 on Ragnaros; Hunter-Gatherer at Level 4 on Rexxar; Hungry for More at Level 1 on Stitches; Viking Hoard as Baseline Quest on The Lost Vikings; Ardent Restoration at Level 1 on Tyrael; Vigor at Leve 1 on Valeera; High King's Quest at Level 1 on Varian; Give Me Twenty at Level 4 on Zarya; Shadow Hunter at Level 1 on Zeratul. The following Talents benefit from Regeneration Globes as well: Lightwell at Level 1 on Anduin; Glimmer of Hope at Level 7 on Auriel; Devil's Due at Level 1 on Diablo; Press Forward at Level 4 on Imperius; Assimilation Mastery at Level 1 on Kerrigan; Ossein Renewal at Level 1 on Leoric; Power Hungry at Level 1 on Li-Ming; Backup Battery at Level 7 on Mei; Spite at Level 4 on Mephisto; Is That a Health Pack?! at Level 4 on Tracer. Due to Aspect of Death, Regeneration Globes are also the only way for allied Heroes to heal Deathwing. 4 Regeneration Globes are almost equivalent to a Healing Fountain.

sections.title: Group Up
sections.text: Auriel asks for assistance! You can use an Assist Ping near you to tell your teammates to group up in a given spot. This is particularly useful when playing a Healer with area of effect healing (for example Auriel).

sections.title: Call Hero
sections.text: Valla wants to help Malfurion Valla asks for assistance! You can use a Quick Ping on an allied Hero followed by an Assist Ping somewhere else to let that Hero know that their help is needed there. This is useful when a Hero cannot do Mercenary Camps alone. Remember to ping beforehand to give them time to react.

sections.title: Defend Ping
sections.text: To use a Defend Ping with the default Hotkeys, you have to press [Alt + Left Mouse Button], move your mouse cursor to the left, and then release. To customize it, look for Quick Ping in the Advanced tab of the Hotkeys window.

sections.title: Defend Town
sections.text: Mephisto wants to defend this Fort! You can use a Defend ping on allied Structure to tell your teammates that more Heroes are needed there to defend it from enemy Minions, Mercenaries, or Heroes. Try to use it as early as possible, otherwise your teammates will not be there in time.

sections.title: Defend Objective
sections.text: Probius wants to secure the area! You can use a Defend ping nearby an Objective to communicate that you would like your team to position in a way that does not let the enemy team get progress on the Objective or to zone them away while someone is capturing it.

sections.title: Mercenary Camp
sections.text: Junkrat wants to defend! You can use a Defend ping nearby a Mercenary Camp to communicate that you would like your team to position in a way that does not let the enemy team invade it or to zone them away while someone is capturing it.

sections.title: Call Hero
sections.text: Li Li wants to help Malfurion Li Li wants to defend! You can use a Quick Ping on an allied Hero followed by a Defend Ping in a lane to let that Hero know that their help is needed there. This is useful when you notice that Structures are taking damage or are going to take damage soon but your Hero is not capable to deal with that or you have something else to do.

sections.title: Retreat Ping
sections.text: To use a Retreat Ping with the default Hotkeys, you have to press the [V] key. To customize it, look for Quick Retreat Ping in the Advanced tab of the Hotkeys window.

sections.title: Fall Back
sections.text: Johanna calls for retreat! You can use a Retreat Ping whenever you feel like it is not the moment to fight for any of the following reasons: numerical disadvantage, lack of resources (low Health and/or Mana), Heroic Abilities on cooldowns, lost Objective, Talent Tier disadvantage, or useless brawl giving free Quest progress to enemy Heroes (such as Zul'jin). When retreating, you should avoid walking on different sides of impassable terrain from your teammates otherwise you will not be able to help each other.

sections.title: Give Objective
sections.text: Chromie calls for retreat! You can use a Retreat Ping when you want to give the Objective to the enemy team because, due to a lack of resources or any other form of disadvantage, your team can no longer win it. If you do not die, at least you will be able to slow down their push with the Objective's reward they won.

sections.title: Abandon Town
sections.text: Nova calls for retreat! You can use a Retreat Ping when you want to abandon a Fort or Keep because, due to a lack of resources or any other form of disadvantage, it can no longer be defended. Dying for a Fort or Keep that is going to be destroyed anyway will only make things worse.

sections.title: Leave Lane
sections.text: Dehaka calls for retreat! You can use a Retreat Ping in a lane when you feel like an allied Hero should not be there, because you are already there and you are fine dealing with Minions or Mercenaries alone. This way your teammates can realize they can go get value elsewhere.

sections.title: Leave Minions
sections.text: Kerrigan calls for retreat! You can use a Retreat Ping nearby enemy Minions to communicate that you wish your teammates to not kill them because you have a Quest that requires last-hitting them. If you kill Minions too quickly, you will slow down their Quest farming, delaying their powerspike. The following Quests require last-hitting Minions: Globe of Annihilation on Azmodan; Ravage's Baseline Quest on Kerrigan; Voodoo Ritual on Nazeebo; Ravenous Hunger at Level 7 on Orphea; Sulfuras Hungers at Level 1 on Ragnaros; Echo of the Elements at Level 1 on Thrall.

sections.title: Ability Ping
sections.text: To use an Ability Ping with the default Hotkeys, you have to press [Alt + Left Mouse Button] on Abilities in the HUD at the bottom of your screen. To customize it, look for Announce Modifier in the Advanced tab of the Hotkeys window.

sections.title: Cooldown
sections.text: Alexstrasza can use Dragonqueen in 35 seconds! You can use an Ability Ping to announce that a given Ability will be ready in x seconds. This is useful to coordinate engage and follow-up, to say that your global is on cooldown, or to tell your teammates that a key Ability is not available yet. Here is a list of key Abilities that are important to announce when not ready: Dragonqueen on Alexstrasza; Leap of Faith on Anduin; Phase Shift on Brightwing; Brushstalker on Dehaka; Flight on Falstad; Bio-Kill Switch on Stukov. At high level of play you may also want to announce the following key Abilities: Soothing Mist on Brightwing; Into the Fray on Garrosh; Let's Go! on Li Li; Nature's Cure on Malfurion; Purge on Rehgar; Hand of Protection on Uther; Intercession on Whitemane. Any engage and follow-up Ability is worth announcing, so that you can better coordinate with your teammates. An engage without follow-up ready is generally going to be a waste. Abilities which require a setup have a higher chance to miss without an engage to keep enemy Heroes in place. Uther is ready to use Divine Shield! You can also use an Ability Ping to announce that a given Ability is ready. This may be useful right before using a Heroic Ability or right after picking a Heroic Ability that requires your team to be aware of it (for example Sanctification on Tyrael). Anduin has 2 charges of Leap of Faith! When using an Ability Ping on an Ability with charges, the game will not only say if it is ready but also the amount of charges currently available. This way you can tell your teammates how many times you could cast an important Ability in during the next fight. Maiev is not able to use Naisha's Memento yet! When using an Ability Ping on an Ability that requires a condition to be met in order to be usable, the game will simply show it is not usable. This may be useful for telling your teammates that you cannot do Mercenary Camps without it (for example Naisha's Memento on Maiev).

sections.title: Low Mana
sections.text: Uther does not have enough Mana for Holy Light! You can use an Ability Ping when not having enough Mana to cast a given Ability to communicate that to your team. This way your teammates will be warned that, despite being alive, you can no longer contribute to the fight.

sections.title: Heroic Ability
sections.text: Anduin is ready to use Lightbomb! You can use an Ability Ping right after choosing your Heroic Ability to tell your teammates which one you picked. This may be useful when you pick a Heroic Ability that requires your team to be aware of it (for example Sanctification on Tyrael).

sections.title: Hero Ping
sections.text: To use a Hero Ping with the default Hotkeys, you have to press [Alt + Left Mouse Button] on Heroes in the HUD at the top of your screen. To customize it, look for Announce Modifier in the Advanced tab of the Hotkeys window.

sections.title: Missing Hero
sections.text: Li Li warns that Genji is missing! You can use a Hero Ping on a missing enemy Hero to tell your teammates to be careful. This is best used when enemy Heroes are rotating from a lane to another or looking for a gank.

sections.title: Dead Hero
sections.text: Nova warns that Muradin will respawn in 9 seconds! You can use a Hero Ping on an enemy Hero to share their respawn time in chat. If their respawn time is high, it means you want to push the advantage; if their respawn time is low, it means you have to be careful because they will respawn soon. Auriel warns that Valla will respawn in 22 seconds! You can use a Hero Ping on an allied Hero to share their respawn time in chat. Regardless of their respawn time, it means you want to play safe until they come back, otherwise you will be outnumbered and you will only risk staggering deaths.

sections.title: Talent Tier Ping
sections.text: To use a Talent Tier Ping with the default Hotkeys, you have to press [Alt + Left Mouse Button] on Team Levels in the HUD at the top of your screen. To customize it, look for Announce Modifier in the Advanced tab of the Hotkeys window.

sections.title: Play Aggressively
sections.text: Arthas notes that your team has a Talent Tier advantage. When your team has a Talent Tier advantage or is close to getting it, you can use a Talent Tier Ping to communicate that you would like to get value from it, by fighting and/or taking down enemy Structures. Note that the enemy team will likely try to avoid fighting.

sections.title: Play Defensively
sections.text: Varian notes that the enemy team has a Talent Tier advantage. When the enemy team has a Talent Tier advantage or is close to getting it, you can use a Talent Tier Ping to communicate that you should soak Experience from Minions and avoid fighting because it will be extremely unlikely to beat them. Note that the enemy team will likely try to force a fight or gank someone.

sections.title: Raise Awareness
sections.text: Varian notes that both teams are on the same Talent Tier. When neither team has a Talent Tier advantage, you can use a Talent Tier Ping to tell your teammates to pay attention to Team Levels. If your team is behind in Experience, it means you want to fight before the enemy team gets a Talent Tier advantage. If your team is ahead in Experience or someone in your team needs an important Talent Tier (for example Varian before Level 4), it means you want to wait for the next Talent Tier to be unlocked.

sections.title: Health Ping
sections.text: To use a Health Ping with the default Hotkeys, you have to press [Alt + Left Mouse Button] on your Health Bar in the HUD at the bottom-left corner of your screen. To customize it, look for Announce Modifier in the Advanced tab of the Hotkeys window.

sections.title: Low Health
sections.text: Tyrael has 12% Health! You can use a Health Ping to communicate that your Health is low. This way your teammates will be warned that, despite being alive, you can no longer contribute to the fight.

sections.title: Resource Ping
sections.text: To use a Resource Ping with the default Hotkeys, you have to press [Alt + Left Mouse Button] on your Resource Bar in the HUD at the bottom-left corner of your screen. To customize it, look for Announce Modifier in the Advanced tab of the Hotkeys window.

sections.title: Low Resource
sections.text: Lt. Morales has 2% Energy! You can use a Resource Ping when playing a Hero with a Resource to communicate that your Mana, Energy, Fury, Rage, or Scrap is low. This way your teammates will be warned that, despite being alive, you cannot contribute to the fight for a while. This is particularly useful if you are the Healer of your team.

guides.title: Lava Wave timings
guides.blurb: When to cast Lava Wave on each map (Ragnaros).

sections.title: Introduction
sections.text: Lava Wave allows you to soak distant lanes while getting Experience from other lanes or while helping allied Heroes. This is possible because Heroes who kill Minions with Abilities or Basic Attacks will automatically collect the Experience from the Minions. Lava Wave always kills Minions when hitting them, so it can reliably be used to soak. What is the best moment to cast Lava Wave if you want to catch as many Minions as possible? The answer is different for almost every lane across all Maps because Lava Wave takes a different amount of time to travel from one side of the battlefield to the opposite one. After casting a lot of Lava Waves, we have managed to extrapolate Lava Wave Timings for each lane on each Map. This guide has been created with the help of Debug Mode, a special Sandbox for all Maps. If you want to test out our Lava Wave timings on a specific Map that is not available as Sandbox in Custom Games, follow the instructions provided in our Debug Mode Guide.

sections.title: Usage
sections.text: You can use the Lava Wave timings provided in this guide to cast Lava Wave when the Game Time shows the corresponding amount of seconds, or a few seconds after that. This way you will maximize the Experience you gain from it and help your team level up faster. Furthermore, catching an extra wave of Minions means you can stay in another lane for 30 seconds longer, getting similar value to global Heroes. When it comes to casting Lava Wave based on Lava Wave timings, being slightly late is not bad because you or an allied Hero will usually be able to soak Experience from enemy Minions that are close to dying from allied Structures or Minions. On the other hand, being too early is not ideal because it could cause Lava Wave to miss the whole next wave of Minions. In some situations you may need to ignore Lava Wave timings and cast Lava Wave for other reasons than soaking as much as Experience as possible: defensively, to quickly kill enemy Minions near allied Structures and deter the enemy team from pushing, or offensively, to deal damage to enemy Heroes who are fighting in lane. The closer to your Core enemy Heroes are, the easier will be to take opponents by surprise.

sections.title: Timings
sections.text: All you have to remember is the first number for every lane on each Map. You do not need to learn the second number because you can easily calculate it by adding 30 seconds to the first number. Considering that Lava Wave has 120 seconds of cooldown and that is divisible by 30 seconds, after timing it for a given lane, you can cast it on cooldown in the same lane. If you do not want to learn all these numbers or if you cannot remember what are the correct Lava Wave timings for a given Map while playing, bookmark this guide. To quickly find what you are looking for, click on the name of the Map you are playing on at the top of the guide and the page will automatically scroll down for you.
